concept.title: Necessity of Uniform Per-Layer Budgets
concept.concept_description:
Depth-additive damage bounds hold under a per-layer perturbation bound that is uniform over upstream states, and fail under any bound certified at a single state. The conjecture upgrades this from a counterexample to a dichotomy for arbitrary budget functionals.

For every per-layer budget functional B that depends only on the behaviour of a layer at finitely many prescribed upstream states, there is a stack on which the joint damage exceeds the sum of the budgets.

Generalise the witness family to interpolate any finite set of probe states, and prove that a masking suffix can always be inserted after the probes.

Serving policies must certify worst-case per-layer behaviour; held-out-window measurements can never be turned into a sound budget.

Some finite probe set suffices, and the design question becomes which probes, opening a concrete experimental programme.

-- NEW_FILE: Catalog/Applications/NET59ProbeBudgets/Basic.lean
import Probability.NET59NonIdentifiability

/-!
# Per-layer budgets: soundness is exactly uniform domination

`Probability.NET59HybridEpistasis` proves that a per-layer perturbation bound
that is *uniform over upstream states* adds up along depth
(`chain_tv_le_depth_mul`), and `Probability.NET59NonIdentifiability` shows that a
bound certified at a *single* state does not.  This file turns the pair of
observations into an exact characterisation.

A **per-layer budget functional** is any map `B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ`
assigning a number to an (intact, pruned) layer pair.  It is **sound** if for
every pair of stacks of equal depth and every input law, the joint damage is at
most the sum of the per-layer budgets.

Main results:

* `budget_sound_of_dominates` — if `B f p ≥ tv (f a) (p a)` for every state `a`
  then `B` is sound (heterogeneous depth-additivity, generalising
  `chain_tv_le_depth_mul`);
* `dominates_of_budget_sound` — conversely every sound budget dominates the
  pointwise channel distance at every state (single-layer stacks with Dirac
  inputs);
* `budget_sound_iff_dominates` — **soundness ⇔ uniform domination**;
* `uniformBudget` (the worst case over states) is sound and is the *least*
  sound budget: `budget_sound_iff_uniform_le`.

So "certify worst-case per-layer behaviour" is not one policy among others: it
is literally the definition of a sound budget.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Small facts about channels -/

/-- Pushing a Dirac mass through a channel evaluates the channel. -/
@[simp] theorem push_dirac [DecidableEq α] (K : Kern α α) (a : α) : push K (dirac a) = K a := by
  refine Dist.ext' fun b => ?_
  simp only [push_apply, dirac]
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a] <;> simp +contextual

/-- Sequential composition of two channels: first `K`, then `G`. -/
def compK (K G : Kern α α) : Kern α α := fun a => push G (K a)

/-- Pushing twice is pushing through the composite channel. -/
theorem push_push (K G : Kern α α) (μ : Dist α) : push G (push K μ) = push (compK K G) μ := by
  refine Dist.ext' fun b => ?_
  simp only [push_apply, compK, Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => by ring

/-- The channel computed by a whole stack. -/
def chainK [DecidableEq α] (L : List (Kern α α)) : Kern α α := fun a => chain L (dirac a)

/-- A stack acts on input laws as the single channel `chainK L`: running a stack
is linear in the input law. -/
theorem chain_eq_push_chainK [DecidableEq α] (L : List (Kern α α)) (μ : Dist α) :
    chain L μ = push (chainK L) μ := by
  induction L generalizing μ with
  | nil =>
      have : chainK ([] : List (Kern α α)) = idK := rfl
      rw [this, push_idK, chain_nil]
  | cons K L ih =>
      have hK : chainK (K :: L) = compK K (chainK L) := by
        funext a
        simp only [chainK, compK, chain_cons, push_dirac]
        exact ih (K a)
      rw [chain_cons, ih, push_push, hK]

/-! ## 2. Budget functionals -/

/-- The total budget charged to a pair of stacks: the sum of the per-layer
budgets, layer by layer. -/
def budgetSum (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : List (Kern α α) → List (Kern α α) → ℚ
  | f :: F, p :: P => B f p + budgetSum B F P
  | _, _ => 0

@[simp] theorem budgetSum_cons (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) (f p : Kern α α)
    (F P : List (Kern α α)) : budgetSum B (f :: F) (p :: P) = B f p + budgetSum B F P := rfl

@[simp] theorem budgetSum_nil (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) (P : List (Kern α α)) :
    budgetSum B [] P = 0 := by cases P <;> rfl

/-- A per-layer budget functional is **sound** if, on every pair of stacks of
equal depth and from every input law, the joint damage never exceeds the sum of
the per-layer budgets. -/
def SoundBudget (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ F P : List (Kern α α), F.length = P.length →
    ∀ μ : Dist α, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) ≤ budgetSum B F P

/-- The contextual hybrid cost is bounded by any budget dominating the
pointwise channel distance. -/
theorem hybridCost_le_budgetSum (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ)
    (hB : ∀ f p : Kern α α, ∀ a, tv (f a) (p a) ≤ B f p) :
    ∀ (F P : List (Kern α α)) (μ : Dist α), hybridCost F P μ ≤ budgetSum B F P := by
  intro F
  induction F with
  | nil => intro P μ; simp
  | cons f F ih =>
      intro P μ
      cases P with
      | nil => simp [hybridCost, budgetSum]
      | cons p P =>
          rw [hybridCost_cons, budgetSum_cons]
          have h1 : tv (push f μ) (push p μ) ≤ B f p :=
            tv_push_perturb_unif f p μ (hB f p)
          have h2 := ih P (push p μ)
          linarith

/-- **Sufficiency (heterogeneous depth-additivity).**  Any budget that dominates
the channel distance at *every* state is sound. -/
theorem budget_sound_of_dominates (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ)
    (hB : ∀ f p : Kern α α, ∀ a, tv (f a) (p a) ≤ B f p) : SoundBudget B := by
  intro F P hlen μ

theorem push_push (K G : Kern α α) (μ : Dist α) : push G (push K μ) = push (compK K G) μ := by

/-!
# The probe-budget dichotomy

A per-layer budget functional `B` *depends only on the behaviour of a layer at
the probe states `S`* (`ProbeLocal S B`) if `B f p = B f' p'` whenever `f, f'`
and `p, p'` have the same responses at every probe.  It is *calibrated* if an
unpruned layer is charged nothing (`B f f = 0`).  Local + calibrated implies
*probe-blind*: a layer pair whose probe responses agree is charged `0`.

Main results:

* `blind_budget_counterexample` — if the probes do not span `ℚ^α` (and `α` has
  two points), then for **every** probe-blind budget and **every** depth `n+1`
  there is a stack pair whose total budget is `0` and whose joint damage, from
  some input, is `1`;
* `blind_budget_not_relaxed_sound` — no multiplicative or additive slack
  (`joint ≤ C · Σ budgets + δ`, `δ < 1`) repairs such a budget;
* `probe_budget_dichotomy` — **there is a sound, calibrated, `S`-local budget
  iff `α` is a singleton or `S` spans**;
* `window_certifies_iff` — a held-out window of inputs on which two stacks agree
  certifies agreement on *all* inputs iff the window spans;
* `small_window_never_certifies` — a window with fewer inputs than states never
  certifies anything: some stack pair is invisible on the window and maximally
  damaged off it.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Probe-local budget functionals -/

/-- `B` depends on a layer pair only through the responses at the probe states. -/
def ProbeLocal (S : Set (Dist α)) (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f p f' p' : Kern α α, AgreeOn S f f' → AgreeOn S p p' → B f p = B f' p'

/-- An unpruned layer is charged nothing. -/
def Calibrated (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop := ∀ f : Kern α α, B f f = 0

/-- A layer pair that no probe can tell apart is charged nothing. -/
def ProbeBlind (S : Set (Dist α)) (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f p : Kern α α, AgreeOn S f p → B f p = 0

/-- Probe-local calibrated budgets are probe-blind. -/
theorem ProbeLocal.blind {S : Set (Dist α)} {B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ}
    (hL : ProbeLocal S B) (hC : Calibrated B) : ProbeBlind S B := by
  intro f p hfp
  rw [hL f p f f (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun s hs => (hfp s hs).symm)]
  exact hC f

/-! ## 2. Stacks built from a witness layer -/

theorem chain_replicate_idK' [DecidableEq α] (n : ℕ) (μ : Dist α) :

  induction n generalizing μ with
  | zero => simp

  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih => rw [List.replicate_succ, budgetSum_cons, ih]; push_cast; ring

/-- **Necessity of uniform budgets, for every probe-blind functional.**  If the
probe states do not span `ℚ^α`, then at every depth there is a stack pair on
which a probe-blind budget charges nothing in total, while the joint damage from
some input law is maximal. -/
theorem blind_budget_counterexample [DecidableEq α] {S : Set (Dist α)} (hS : ¬ Spans S)
    {x y : α} (hxy : x ≠ y) (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) (hB : ProbeBlind S B) (n : ℕ) :

/-- The Dirac-sum budget `Σ_a tv (f a) (p a)`; it dominates the uniform budget and

def diracSumBudget (f p : Kern α α) : ℚ := ∑ a, tv (f a) (p a)

theorem diracSumBudget_sound : SoundBudget (diracSumBudget (α := α)) :=

theorem probe_budget_dichotomy [DecidableEq α] (S : Set (Dist α)) :
    (∃ B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ, ProbeLocal S B ∧ Calibrated B ∧ SoundBudget B) ↔

    obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := exists_pair_ne α
    obtain ⟨F, P, hF, hP, h0, μ, h1⟩ :=
      blind_budget_counterexample hspan hxy B (hL.blind hC) 0
    have := hsound F P (by rw [hF, hP]) μ
    rw [h0, h1] at this
    norm_num at this
  · intro h
    have hsep : Separates S := (separates_iff S).2 h
    refine ⟨diracSumBudget, ?_, ?_, diracSumBudget_sound⟩
    · intro f p f' p' hf hp
      rw [hsep f f' hf, hsep p p' hp]
    · intro f
      simp [diracSumBudget]

/-- **A finite probe set suffices.**  The `|α|` Dirac probes carry a sound,
calibrated, probe-local budget — namely the uniform worst-case budget. -/
theorem diracProbes_suffice [DecidableEq α] :
    ∃ B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ,
      ProbeLocal (Set.range (dirac : α → Dist α)) B ∧ Calibrated B ∧ SoundBudget B :=
  (probe_budget_dichotomy _).2 (Or.inr diracProbes_spans)

/-- **Probe count lower bound.**  If a family of `m` probe states supports a
sound calibrated probe-local budget on a state space with at least two points,
then `m ≥ |α|`. -/
theorem probe_count_lower_bound [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α] {m : ℕ}
    (probes : Fin m → Dist α)
    (h : ∃ B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ,
      ProbeLocal (Set.range probes) B ∧ Calibrated B ∧ SoundBudget B) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ m := by
  rcases (probe_budget_dichotomy _).1 h with hs | hs
  · exact absurd hs (not_subsingleton α)
  · exact card_le_of_spans probes hs

/-! ## 4. Held-out windows -/

/-- **Window dichotomy.**  Agreement of two stacks on every input of a held-out
window certifies agreement on all inputs if and only if the window spans (or the
state space is trivial). -/
theorem window_certifies_iff [DecidableEq α] (W : Set (Dist α)) :
    (∀ F P : List (Kern α α), (∀ w ∈ W, chain F w = chain P w) →
        ∀ μ : Dist α, chain F μ = chain P μ) ↔ Subsingleton α ∨ Spans W := by
  rw [← separates_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h g q hgq
    funext a
    have := h [g] [q] (fun w hw => by simpa using hgq w hw) (dirac a)
    simpa using this
  · intro hsep F P hFP μ
    have hK : chainK F = chainK P := hsep _ _ fun w hw => by
      rw [← chain_eq_push_chainK, ← chain_eq_push_chainK]; exact hFP w hw
    rw [chain_eq_push_chainK, chain_eq_push_chainK, hK]

/-- **Small windows never certify.**  If a held-out window has fewer inputs than
there are states, some depth-`n+1` stack pair is exactly invisible on the window
(identical outputs at every window input) yet does maximal damage at some other
input.  (`Nontrivial α` is needed: on a one-point space nothing can be damaged.) -/
theorem small_window_never_certifies [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α] {m : ℕ} (window : Fin m → Dist α)
    (hm : m < Fintype.card α) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ F P : List (Kern α α), F.length = n + 1 ∧ P.length = n + 1 ∧
      (∀ i, chain F (window i) = chain P (window i)) ∧
      ∃ μ : Dist α, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) = 1 := by
  have hspan : ¬ Spans (Set.range window) := fun h => absurd (card_le_of_spans window h) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := exists_pair_ne α
  obtain ⟨g, q, hgq, a, ha⟩ := exists_blind_pair hspan hxy
  refine ⟨g :: List.replicate n idK, q :: List.replicate n idK, by simp, by simp, ?_,
    dirac a, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    rw [chain_cons, chain_cons, chain_replicate_idK', chain_replicate_idK']
    exact hgq _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
  · rw [chain_cons, chain_cons, chain_replicate_idK', chain_replicate_idK', push_dirac,
      push_dirac, ha]

end Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

import Applications.NET59ProbeBudgets.Dichotomy

/-!
# Masking suffixes: every pruning instance hides from every solo probe

`Probability.NET59NonIdentifiability` exhibits one witness family
(`fullStack` / `prunedStack` on `Fin 2`, probed at the single input `d0`) whose
solo profile vanishes while the joint damage is any prescribed `t`.  Here the
construction is turned into a *universal transformation*.

`maskStack F d` / `maskPruned P d` wrap an arbitrary intact stack `F` and pruned
stack `P` between

* a **collapsing prefix** `constK d` (shared by both stacks), which sends every
  upstream state to the probe state `d`, and
* a **masking suffix**: the intact stack ends with the forgetful layer
  `constK (chain F d)`, the pruned stack with the transparent layer `idK`.

`masking_suffix` proves, for **every** input law `μ` (so in particular for every
finite or infinite set of probe inputs, spanning or not):

* the joint damage of the wrapped pair equals the original joint damage
  `tv (chain F d) (chain P d)`, and
* the solo profile of the wrapped pair is identically `0`.

So no budget computed from solo (one-layer-at-a-time, output-level) measurements
— at any number of probe inputs — can bound joint damage
(`solo_certificate_unsound`).  Every pruning instance, however damaging, can be
made invisible to solo probing at the cost of two extra layers.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-- The wrapped intact stack: collapse to `d`, run `F`, then forget everything
and output the intact answer `chain F d`. -/
def maskStack (F : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) : List (Kern α α) :=
  constK d :: (F ++ [constK (chain F d)])

/-- The wrapped pruned stack: collapse to `d`, run `P`, then pass through. -/
def maskPruned [DecidableEq α] (P : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) : List (Kern α α) :=
  constK d :: (P ++ [idK])

theorem length_maskStack (F : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) :
    (maskStack F d).length = F.length + 2 := by simp [maskStack]

theorem length_maskPruned [DecidableEq α] (P : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) :
    (maskPruned P d).length = P.length + 2 := by simp [maskPruned]

/-- The wrapped intact stack outputs `chain F d` from every input. -/
theorem chain_maskStack (F : List (Kern α α)) (d μ : Dist α) :
    chain (maskStack F d) μ = chain F d := by
  rw [maskStack, chain_cons, chain_snoc_constK]

/-- The wrapped pruned stack outputs `chain P d` from every input. -/
theorem chain_maskPruned [DecidableEq α] (P : List (Kern α α)) (d μ : Dist α) :
    chain (maskPruned P d) μ = chain P d := by
  rw [maskPruned, chain_cons, push_constK, chain_append, chain_cons, chain_nil, push_idK]

/-- Ablating any single layer of the wrapped intact stack leaves its output
unchanged, from every input. -/
theorem chain_maskStack_set [DecidableEq α] (F P : List (Kern α α))
    (hlen : F.length = P.length) (d μ : Dist α) (j : ℕ) :
    chain ((maskStack F d).set j ((maskPruned P d).getD j idK)) μ = chain F d := by
  rcases j with _ | i
  · -- the collapsing prefix is shared, so ablating it changes nothing
    simp only [maskStack, maskPruned, List.getD_cons_zero, List.set_cons_zero]
    rw [chain_cons, chain_snoc_constK]
  · simp only [maskStack, maskPruned, List.getD_cons_succ, List.set_cons_succ, chain_cons,
      push_constK]
    rcases lt_trichotomy i F.length with hi | hi | hi
    · -- an inner layer: the forgetful suffix masks it
      rw [List.set_append_left _ _ hi, chain_snoc_constK]
    · -- the suffix itself: replacing it by `idK` reproduces the intact output
      subst hi
      have hg : (P ++ [idK]).getD F.length idK = idK := by
        rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD]
        rcases h : (P ++ [idK])[F.length]? with _ | k
        · rfl
        · rw [hlen, List.getElem?_append_right le_rfl] at h
          simp at h
          simp [h]
      rw [hg, List.set_append_right _ _ le_rfl]
      simp [chain_append]
    · -- out of range: nothing is replaced
      rw [List.set_eq_of_length_le (by simp; omega), chain_snoc_constK]

/-- **Masking-suffix theorem.**  For every intact stack `F`, every pruned stack
`P` of the same depth and every probe state `d`, the wrapped pair
`maskStack F d` / `maskPruned P d`

* has the same depth (two more layers),
* has joint damage exactly `tv (chain F d) (chain P d)` from **every** input,
* has solo profile identically `0` from **every** input. -/
theorem masking_suffix [DecidableEq α] (F P : List (Kern α α)) (hlen : F.length = P.length)
    (d : Dist α) :
    (maskStack F d).length = (maskPruned P d).length ∧
    (∀ μ : Dist α, tv (chain (maskStack F d) μ) (chain (maskPruned P d) μ)
        = tv (chain F d) (chain P d)) ∧
    (∀ μ : Dist α, ∀ j : ℕ,
        tv (chain (maskStack F d) μ)
          (chain ((maskStack F d).set j ((maskPruned P d).getD j idK)) μ) = 0) := by
  refine ⟨by rw [length_maskStack, length_maskPruned, hlen], fun μ => ?_, fun μ j => ?_⟩
  · rw [chain_maskStack, chain_maskPruned]
  · rw [chain_maskStack, chain_maskStack_set F P hlen, tv_self]

/-- The solo profile of a stack pair at input `μ`: the output-level damage of
ablating layer `j` alone. -/
def soloCost [DecidableEq α] (F P : List (Kern α α)) (μ : Dist α) (j : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  tv (chain F μ) (chain (F.set j (P.getD j idK)) μ)

/-- **Generalised witness family.**  For any two laws `d, c` and any depth
`n + 3`, there is a stack pair whose solo profile vanishes at every input and
every layer, while its joint damage is `tv d c` at every input.  On `Fin 2`
with `d = d0` and `c = bern t` this recovers the NET-59 witness family, now
uniformly over all inputs instead of at the single probe `d0`. -/
theorem witness_family [DecidableEq α] (d c : Dist α) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ F P : List (Kern α α), F.length = n + 3 ∧ P.length = n + 3 ∧
      (∀ μ j, soloCost F P μ j = 0) ∧ (∀ μ, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) = tv d c) := by
  obtain ⟨hl, hjoint, hsolo⟩ := masking_suffix (List.replicate (n + 1) (idK : Kern α α))
    (List.replicate (n + 1) (constK c)) (by simp) d
  refine ⟨_, _, by rw [length_maskStack]; simp, by rw [length_maskPruned]; simp, hsolo,
    fun μ => ?_⟩
  rw [hjoint μ, chain_replicate_idK', chain_replicate_constK]

/-- **Solo certificates are unsound, at any set of probe inputs.**  Let `Φ` be any
rule turning the solo profiles of a stack pair (observed at any family of probe
inputs, finite or not) into a damage certificate, subject only to `Φ` returning
`0` on an identically zero profile.  If `α` has two points, `Φ` certifies `0` for
some stack pair whose joint damage is `1` at every input. -/
theorem solo_certificate_unsound [DecidableEq α] {ι : Type*} (probes : ι → Dist α)
    (Φ : (ι → ℕ → ℚ) → ℚ) (hΦ : Φ (fun _ _ => 0) = 0) {x y : α} (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    ∃ F P : List (Kern α α), F.length = P.length ∧
      Φ (fun i j => soloCost F P (probes i) j) = 0 ∧
      ∀ μ, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨F, P, hF, hP, hsolo, hjoint⟩ := witness_family (dirac x) (dirac y) 0
  refine ⟨F, P, by rw [hF, hP], ?_, fun μ => by rw [hjoint μ, tv_dirac_ne hxy]⟩
  have : (fun i j => soloCost F P (probes i) j) = fun _ _ => 0 := by
    funext i j; exact hsolo _ _
  rw [this, hΦ]

/-! ## Lab notes

The NET-59 parameters: `Fin 2`, probe `d0`, target `t = 17/1000`.  The masked
witness has depth `n + 3`; its solo profile is `0` at every input and its joint
damage is `17/1000` at every input — not just at the single input `d0` probed by
the original family. -/

example (n : ℕ) : ∃ F P : List (Kern (Fin 2) (Fin 2)), F.length = n + 3 ∧ P.length = n + 3 ∧
    (∀ μ j, soloCost F P μ j = 0) ∧ (∀ μ, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) = 17 / 1000) := by
  obtain ⟨F, P, h1, h2, h3, h4⟩ := witness_family d0 (bern (17 / 1000) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)) n
  refine ⟨F, P, h1, h2, h3, fun μ => ?_⟩
  rw [h4, d0, tv_bern]; norm_num

end Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

/-!
# Which probes?  Trajectory budgets and design coefficients

The dichotomy (`probe_budget_dichotomy`) says a probe set supports a sound
budget iff it spans.  This file makes the positive side *quantitative and
constructive*, which is what an experimental programme needs, and pins down the
exact boundary of the negative side.

## Trajectory budgets (the sharp edge of the dichotomy)

* `joint_le_trajectoryCost` — for a **fixed input** `μ`, the joint damage is at
  most the sum of the layer-output perturbations measured at the **intact
  upstream states of that same input**.  So a per-layer measurement taken on the
  input's own intact trajectory *is* sound for that input; what fails is reusing
  it for other inputs.
* `trajectory_window_dichotomy` — zero trajectory cost on every input of a
  held-out window certifies zero damage on **all** inputs iff the window spans.

## Design coefficients (the positive side, made quantitative)

* `tv_push_le_combination` — if `v = Σ cᵢ sᵢ` as signed measures, the
  perturbation of a layer at `v` is at most `Σ |cᵢ|` times its perturbations at
  the probes `sᵢ`;
* `designBudget_sound` — given probes `s` and coefficients `c` writing every
  Dirac state as `Σ c a i • s i`, the **design budget**
  `Σ_a Σ_i |c a i| · tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i))` is probe-local,
  calibrated and sound: an explicit sound budget computed from probe
  measurements only;
* `window_extrapolation` — the same coefficients extrapolate joint damage from a
  held-out window to any input in its span, with amplification `Σ |cᵢ|`.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Trajectory costs -/

/-- The trajectory cost of a stack pair at input `μ`: layer `j` is charged the
perturbation of its *own output* at the intact upstream state of `μ`. -/
def trajectoryCost : List (Kern α α) → List (Kern α α) → Dist α → ℚ
  | f :: F, p :: P, μ => tv (push f μ) (push p μ) + trajectoryCost F P (push f μ)
  | _, _, _ => 0

@[simp] theorem trajectoryCost_cons (f p : Kern α α) (F P : List (Kern α α)) (μ : Dist α) :
    trajectoryCost (f :: F) (p :: P) μ = tv (push f μ) (push p μ) + trajectoryCost F P (push f μ) :=
  rfl

/-- **Trajectory bound.**  At a fixed input, joint damage is at most the sum of the
per-layer output perturbations measured along the intact trajectory of that
input.  (Compare `chain_hybrid_bound`, which measures along the *pruned*
trajectory, inaccessible to an experimenter who only runs the intact model.) -/
theorem joint_le_trajectoryCost :
    ∀ (F P : List (Kern α α)), F.length = P.length →
      ∀ μ : Dist α, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) ≤ trajectoryCost F P μ := by
  intro F
  induction F with
  | nil => intro P hlen μ; cases P with
    | nil => simp [trajectoryCost]
    | cons p P => simp at hlen
  | cons f F ih =>
      intro P hlen μ
      cases P with
      | nil => simp at hlen
      | cons p P =>
          rw [chain_cons, chain_cons, trajectoryCost_cons]
          have h1 := tv_triangle (chain F (push f μ)) (chain P (push f μ)) (chain P (push p μ))
          have h2 := ih P (by simpa using hlen) (push f μ)
          have h3 := tv_chain_le P (push f μ) (push p μ)
          linarith

/-- Zero trajectory cost forces zero damage at that input. -/
theorem chain_eq_of_trajectoryCost_eq_zero (F P : List (Kern α α)) (hlen : F.length = P.length)
    (μ : Dist α) (h : trajectoryCost F P μ = 0) : chain F μ = chain P μ := by
  have := joint_le_trajectoryCost F P hlen μ
  rw [h] at this
  exact (tv_eq_zero_iff _ _).1 (le_antisymm this (tv_nonneg _ _))

/-- **Trajectory-window dichotomy.**  Requiring every pruned layer to reproduce its
intact counterpart along the intact trajectories of a held-out window certifies
the pruned stack on *all* inputs iff the window spans (or `α` is trivial).
Held-out-window measurements are sound *on the window*
(`joint_le_trajectoryCost`); they extrapolate exactly when the window spans. -/
theorem trajectory_window_dichotomy [DecidableEq α] (W : Set (Dist α)) :
    (∀ F P : List (Kern α α), F.length = P.length →
        (∀ w ∈ W, trajectoryCost F P w = 0) → ∀ μ : Dist α, chain F μ = chain P μ) ↔
      Subsingleton α ∨ Spans W := by
  rw [← window_certifies_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [window_certifies_iff, ← separates_iff]
    intro g q hgq
    funext a
    have := h [g] [q] rfl (fun w hw => by simp [trajectoryCost, hgq w hw]) (dirac a)
    simpa using this
  · intro h F P hlen hW μ
    exact h F P (fun w hw => chain_eq_of_trajectoryCost_eq_zero F P hlen w (hW w hw)) μ

/-! ## 2. Signed combinations of probes -/

/-- **Combination inequality.**  If `v.p = Σᵢ cᵢ • (s i).p`, then the perturbation
of a layer at `v` is controlled by its perturbations at the probes, weighted by
`|cᵢ|`. -/
theorem tv_push_le_combination {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f p : Kern α α) (s : ι → Dist α)
    (c : ι → ℚ) (v : Dist α) (hv : v.p = ∑ i, c i • (s i).p) :
    tv (push f v) (push p v) ≤ ∑ i, |c i| * tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i)) := by
  have hdiff : ∀ b, (push f v).p b - (push p v).p b
      = ∑ i, c i * ((push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b) := by
    intro b
    have e1 : (push f v).p b = ∑ i, c i * (push f (s i)).p b := by
      rw [← pushL_dist, hv, map_sum]
      simp only [map_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, pushL_dist]
    have e2 : (push p v).p b = ∑ i, c i * (push p (s i)).p b := by
      rw [← pushL_dist, hv, map_sum]
      simp only [map_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, pushL_dist]
    rw [e1, e2, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
  have hb : ∀ b, |(push f v).p b - (push p v).p b|
      ≤ ∑ i, |c i| * |(push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b| := by
    intro b
    rw [hdiff b]
    refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => abs_mul _ _
  unfold tv
  have hsum := Finset.sum_le_sum fun b (_ : b ∈ Finset.univ) => hb b
  rw [Finset.sum_comm] at hsum
  have : ∑ i, |c i| * ((∑ b, |(push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b|) / 2)
      = (∑ i, ∑ b, |c i| * |(push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b|) / 2 := by
    rw [Finset.sum_div]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [mul_div_assoc', Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [this]
  linarith

/-! ## 3. Design budgets -/

/-- The design budget of a probe family `s` with Dirac-representing coefficients
`c`: computed from the probe responses only. -/
def designBudget {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (s : ι → Dist α) (c : α → ι → ℚ)
    (f p : Kern α α) : ℚ :=
  ∑ a, ∑ i, |c a i| * tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i))

/-- **Constructive sufficiency.**  If the coefficients `c` write every Dirac state
as a signed combination of the probes, the design budget is probe-local,
calibrated and sound. -/
theorem designBudget_sound [DecidableEq α] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (s : ι → Dist α)
    (c : α → ι → ℚ) (hc : ∀ a, (dirac a).p = ∑ i, c a i • (s i).p) :
    ProbeLocal (Set.range s) (designBudget s c) ∧ Calibrated (designBudget s c) ∧
      SoundBudget (designBudget s c) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro f p f' p' hf hp
    unfold designBudget
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [hf (s i) ⟨i, rfl⟩, hp (s i) ⟨i, rfl⟩]
  · intro f; simp [designBudget]
  · refine budget_sound_of_dominates _ fun f p a => ?_
    have h1 := tv_push_le_combination f p s (c a) (dirac a) (hc a)
    rw [push_dirac, push_dirac] at h1
    refine h1.trans ?_
    exact Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun a => ∑ i, |c a i| * tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i)))
      (fun a _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => mul_nonneg (abs_nonneg _) (tv_nonneg _ _))
      (Finset.mem_univ a)

/-- With the Dirac probes and identity coefficients the design budget is the
Dirac-sum budget: the canonical design. -/
theorem designBudget_dirac [DecidableEq α] (f p : Kern α α) :
    designBudget (dirac : α → Dist α) (fun a i => if a = i then 1 else 0) f p
      = diracSumBudget f p := by
  unfold designBudget diracSumBudget
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a] <;> simp +contextual [push_dirac, eq_comm]

/-- **Window extrapolation.**  If an input `μ` is a signed combination
`Σ cᵢ wᵢ` of held-out window inputs, its joint damage is at most `Σ |cᵢ|` times
the trajectory costs measured on the window.  The `ℓ¹` size of the coefficients
is the amplification factor of the probe design. -/
theorem window_extrapolation [DecidableEq α] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (F P : List (Kern α α)) (hlen : F.length = P.length) (w : ι → Dist α) (c : ι → ℚ)
    (μ : Dist α) (hμ : μ.p = ∑ i, c i • (w i).p) :
    tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) ≤ ∑ i, |c i| * trajectoryCost F P (w i) := by
  rw [chain_eq_push_chainK, chain_eq_push_chainK]
  refine (tv_push_le_combination _ _ w c μ hμ).trans ?_
  refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (abs_nonneg _)
  rw [← chain_eq_push_chainK, ← chain_eq_push_chainK]
  exact joint_le_trajectoryCost F P hlen (w i)

/-! ## 4. Lab notes

Exact data on `Fin 2`.

{bern 1/2}                no       idK vs flipK: equal at the probe, tv at d0 = 1
{bern 1/4, bern 3/4}      yes      d0 = 3/2·bern 1/4 − 1/2·bern 3/4   (ℓ¹ amplification 2)

section LabNotes

/-- A balanced held-out probe cannot tell the identity from a full flip. -/
example : push idK (bern (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num))
      = push flipK (bern (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)) ∧
    tv ((idK : Kern (Fin 2) (Fin 2)) 0) (flipK 0) = 1 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [push_idK, push_flipK]; congr 1; norm_num
  · have h1 : (idK : Kern (Fin 2) (Fin 2)) 0 = dirac 0 := rfl
    have h2 : flipK 0 = dirac 1 := by simp [flipK]
    rw [h1, h2, tv_dirac_ne (by decide)]

/-- The probe pair `bern 1/4`, `bern 3/4` spans, with explicit coefficients. -/
theorem lab_d0_combination :
    (d0).p = (3 / 2 : ℚ) • (bern (1 / 4) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)).p
      + (-1 / 2 : ℚ) • (bern (3 / 4) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)).p := by
  funext b; fin_cases b <;> simp [d0, bern] <;> norm_num

/-- Window extrapolation with amplification `2`: the joint damage from `d0` of
any pruned stack is at most `3/2` times its trajectory cost at `bern 1/4` plus
`1/2` times its trajectory cost at `bern 3/4`. -/
example (F P : List (Kern (Fin 2) (Fin 2))) (hlen : F.length = P.length) :

        + 1 / 2 * trajectoryCost F P (bern (3 / 4) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)) := by
  have h := window_extrapolation F P hlen
    (![bern (1 / 4) (by norm_num) (by norm_num), bern (3 / 4) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)])
    ![3 / 2, -1 / 2] d0 (by rw [lab_d0_combination]; simp [Fin.sum_univ_two])
  simp only [Fin.sum_univ_two, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one] at h
  norm_num [abs_of_pos, abs_of_neg] at h

import Applications.NET59ProbeBudgets.Basic

/-!
# Which probe sets see a layer?  The linear algebra of probing

A budget that "depends only on the behaviour of a layer at prescribed upstream
states" sees a channel `K` only through the probe responses `push K s`,
`s ∈ S`.  Because `push K` is *linear* in the input law, what a probe set can
see is governed by the linear span of the probe vectors `s.p ∈ ℚ^α`.

* `separates_of_spans` — if the probe vectors span `ℚ^α`, two channels with the
  same probe responses are equal;
* `exists_blind_pair` — **witness interpolation**: if the probe vectors do *not*
  span `ℚ^α` (and `α` has two points), there are two channels with identical
  responses at *every* probe whose outputs at some state are mutually singular
  (`tv = 1`).  The construction takes a nonzero linear functional `φ`
  annihilating the probes, normalises its coefficient vector `w` to `u` with
  `max |u| = 1`, and mixes two point masses with weights `(1 ± u a)/2`;
* `separates_iff` — a probe set separates channels **iff** `α` is a singleton
  or the probes span;
* `diracProbes_spans`, `card_le_of_spans` — the `|α|` Dirac probes span, and no
  family of fewer than `|α|` probes does.  So a finite probe set that suffices
  exists, and its minimum size is exactly the number of states.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Probe vectors and their span -/

/-- The span of the probe vectors `s.p` of a set of probe states. -/
def probeSpan (S : Set (Dist α)) : Submodule ℚ (α → ℚ) := Submodule.span ℚ (Dist.p '' S)

/-- A probe set *spans* if its probe vectors span all of `ℚ^α`. -/
def Spans (S : Set (Dist α)) : Prop := probeSpan S = ⊤

/-- Two channels *agree on* a probe set if they have the same response at every
probe state. -/
def AgreeOn (S : Set (Dist α)) (f p : Kern α α) : Prop := ∀ s ∈ S, push f s = push p s

/-- A probe set *separates* channels if agreeing on it forces equality. -/
def Separates (S : Set (Dist α)) : Prop := ∀ f p : Kern α α, AgreeOn S f p → f = p

/-- The pushforward through a channel, extended linearly to all of `ℚ^α`. -/
def pushL (K : Kern α α) : (α → ℚ) →ₗ[ℚ] (α → ℚ) where
  toFun v b := ∑ a, v a * (K a).p b
  map_add' v w := by
    funext b; simp only [Pi.add_apply, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  map_smul' c v := by
    funext b; simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]

theorem pushL_dist (K : Kern α α) (s : Dist α) : pushL K s.p = (push K s).p := rfl

theorem pushL_single [DecidableEq α] (K : Kern α α) (a : α) :
    pushL K (fun x => if x = a then 1 else 0) = (K a).p := by
  funext b
  change ∑ x, (if x = a then (1 : ℚ) else 0) * (K x).p b = (K a).p b
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a] <;> simp +contextual

/-! ## 2. Spanning probe sets separate -/

/-- **Spanning probes see everything.**  If the probe vectors span `ℚ^α`, two
channels with identical probe responses are identical. -/
theorem separates_of_spans {S : Set (Dist α)} (hS : Spans S) : Separates S := by
  classical
  intro f p hfp
  have hle : probeSpan S ≤ LinearMap.ker (pushL f - pushL p) := by
    rw [probeSpan, Submodule.span_le]
    rintro _ ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
    simp only [SetLike.mem_coe, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, pushL_dist, hfp s hs,
      sub_self]
  rw [hS] at hle
  funext a
  have hmem : (fun x => if x = a then (1 : ℚ) else 0) ∈ LinearMap.ker (pushL f - pushL p) :=
    hle Submodule.mem_top
  rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero, pushL_single, pushL_single] at hmem
  exact Dist.ext' fun b => congrFun hmem b

/-! ## 3. Two-point mixtures -/

/-- The mixture `θ μ + (1-θ) ν`. -/
def mix (θ : ℚ) (h0 : 0 ≤ θ) (h1 : θ ≤ 1) (μ ν : Dist α) : Dist α where
  p b := θ * μ.p b + (1 - θ) * ν.p b
  nonneg b := add_nonneg (mul_nonneg h0 (μ.nonneg b)) (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (ν.nonneg b))
  sum_one := by
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum, μ.sum_one, ν.sum_one]; ring

/-- Mixtures of the same two laws are `|θ - θ'| · tv μ ν` apart. -/
theorem tv_mix (θ θ' : ℚ) (h0 h1 h0' h1') (μ ν : Dist α) :
    tv (mix θ h0 h1 μ ν) (mix θ' h0' h1' μ ν) = |θ - θ'| * tv μ ν := by
  unfold tv
  have : ∀ b, |(mix θ h0 h1 μ ν).p b - (mix θ' h0' h1' μ ν).p b| = |θ - θ'| * |μ.p b - ν.p b| := by
    intro b
    rw [← abs_mul]; congr 1; simp only [mix]; ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => this b, ← Finset.mul_sum]; ring

/-- Distinct point masses are at total variation distance `1`. -/
theorem tv_dirac_ne [DecidableEq α] {x y : α} (hxy : x ≠ y) : tv (dirac x) (dirac y) = 1 := by
  refine le_antisymm (tv_le_one _ _) ?_
  unfold tv
  have hsub : ∑ b ∈ ({x, y} : Finset α), |(dirac x).p b - (dirac y).p b|
      ≤ ∑ b, |(dirac x).p b - (dirac y).p b| :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _) fun _ _ _ => abs_nonneg _
  rw [Finset.sum_pair hxy] at hsub
  simp [dirac, hxy, Ne.symm hxy] at hsub
  simp only [dirac]
  linarith

/-- The response of a "state-dependent mixture" channel `a ↦ mix (θ a) μ ν` to a
probe `s` is the mixture with the `s`-averaged weight. -/
theorem push_mixK_p (θ : α → ℚ) (h0 : ∀ a, 0 ≤ θ a) (h1 : ∀ a, θ a ≤ 1) (μ ν s : Dist α)
    (b : α) :
    (push (fun a => mix (θ a) (h0 a) (h1 a) μ ν) s).p b
      = (∑ a, s.p a * θ a) * μ.p b + (1 - ∑ a, s.p a * θ a) * ν.p b := by
  simp only [push_apply, mix]
  have h : ∑ a, s.p a * ν.p b = ν.p b := by rw [← Finset.sum_mul, s.sum_one, one_mul]
  have e : ∑ a, s.p a * (θ a * μ.p b + (1 - θ a) * ν.p b)
      = (∑ a, s.p a * θ a) * μ.p b + ∑ a, s.p a * ν.p b - (∑ a, s.p a * θ a) * ν.p b := by
    rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.sum_mul, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by ring
  rw [e, h]; ring

/-! ## 4. Witness interpolation through any non-spanning probe set -/

/-- **Witness interpolation.**  If the probe vectors fail to span `ℚ^α` and `α`
has two distinct points, there are channels `g, q` that agree at *every* probe
state but whose outputs at some state are mutually singular. -/
theorem exists_blind_pair [DecidableEq α] {S : Set (Dist α)} (hS : ¬ Spans S)
    {x y : α} (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    ∃ g q : Kern α α, AgreeOn S g q ∧ ∃ a, tv (g a) (q a) = 1 := by
  -- a nonzero functional annihilating the probes
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ0, hφ⟩ := Submodule.exists_le_ker_of_lt_top (probeSpan S) (lt_top_iff_ne_top.2 hS)
  set w : α → ℚ := fun a => φ (fun j => if a = j then 1 else 0) with hw
  have hφw : ∀ v, φ v = ∑ a, v a * w a := by
    intro v; rw [LinearMap.pi_apply_eq_sum_univ φ v]; simp [hw, smul_eq_mul]
  have hann : ∀ s ∈ S, ∑ a, s.p a * w a = 0 := by
    intro s hs
    rw [← hφw]
    exact hφ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩)
  -- normalise
  have hne : (Finset.univ : Finset α).Nonempty := ⟨x, Finset.mem_univ x⟩
  obtain ⟨a₀, -, ha₀⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image Finset.univ (fun a => |w a|) hne
  have hM : 0 < |w a₀| := by
    by_contra hle
    push_neg at hle
    apply hφ0
    refine LinearMap.ext fun v => ?_
    rw [hφw, LinearMap.zero_apply]
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a _ => ?_
    have : |w a| ≤ 0 := (ha₀ a (Finset.mem_univ a)).trans hle
    rw [abs_nonpos_iff.1 this, mul_zero]
  set M := |w a₀|
  set u : α → ℚ := fun a => w a / M with hu
  have hu_abs : ∀ a, |u a| ≤ 1 := by
    intro a
    rw [hu]; dsimp only
    rw [abs_div, abs_of_pos hM, div_le_one hM]
    exact ha₀ a (Finset.mem_univ a)
  have hu0 : |u a₀| = 1 := by
    rw [hu]; dsimp only; rw [abs_div, abs_of_pos hM, div_self hM.ne']
  have hlo : ∀ a, -1 ≤ u a := fun a => (abs_le.1 (hu_abs a)).1
  have hhi : ∀ a, u a ≤ 1 := fun a => (abs_le.1 (hu_abs a)).2
  let θg : α → ℚ := fun a => (1 + u a) / 2
  let θq : α → ℚ := fun a => (1 - u a) / 2
  have hg0 : ∀ a, 0 ≤ θg a := fun a => by have := hlo a; simp only [θg]; linarith
  have hg1 : ∀ a, θg a ≤ 1 := fun a => by have := hhi a; simp only [θg]; linarith
  have hq0 : ∀ a, 0 ≤ θq a := fun a => by have := hhi a; simp only [θq]; linarith
  have hq1 : ∀ a, θq a ≤ 1 := fun a => by have := hlo a; simp only [θq]; linarith
  refine ⟨fun a => mix (θg a) (hg0 a) (hg1 a) (dirac x) (dirac y),
    fun a => mix (θq a) (hq0 a) (hq1 a) (dirac x) (dirac y), ?_, a₀, ?_⟩
  · intro s hs
    have hsu : ∑ a, s.p a * u a = 0 := by
      simp only [hu, mul_div_assoc', ← Finset.sum_div, hann s hs, zero_div]
    have hg : ∑ a, s.p a * θg a = 1 / 2 := by
      have : ∑ a, s.p a * θg a = (∑ a, s.p a + ∑ a, s.p a * u a) / 2 := by
        rw [add_div, Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by simp only [θg]; ring
      rw [this, s.sum_one, hsu]; norm_num
    have hq : ∑ a, s.p a * θq a = 1 / 2 := by
      have : ∑ a, s.p a * θq a = (∑ a, s.p a - ∑ a, s.p a * u a) / 2 := by
        rw [sub_div, Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by simp only [θq]; ring
      rw [this, s.sum_one, hsu]; norm_num
    refine Dist.ext' fun b => ?_
    rw [push_mixK_p, push_mixK_p, hg, hq]
  · rw [tv_mix, tv_dirac_ne hxy, mul_one]
    simp only [θg, θq]
    rw [show (1 + u a₀) / 2 - (1 - u a₀) / 2 = u a₀ by ring, hu0]

/-! ## 5. The separation dichotomy -/

/-- On a singleton state space there is only one law. -/
theorem dist_subsingleton [Subsingleton α] (μ ν : Dist α) : μ = ν := by
  refine Dist.ext' fun a => ?_
  have hμ := μ.sum_one; have hν := ν.sum_one
  rw [Fintype.sum_subsingleton _ a] at hμ hν
  rw [hμ, hν]

/-- **Separation dichotomy.**  A set of probe states determines every channel
from its probe responses if and only if the state space is a singleton or the
probe vectors span `ℚ^α`. -/
theorem separates_iff [DecidableEq α] (S : Set (Dist α)) :
    Separates S ↔ Subsingleton α ∨ Spans S := by
  constructor
  · intro hsep
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    obtain ⟨hns, hspan⟩ := h
    obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := exists_pair_ne α
    obtain ⟨g, q, hgq, a, ha⟩ := exists_blind_pair hspan hxy
    rw [hsep g q hgq, tv_self] at ha
    exact zero_ne_one ha
  · rintro (h | h)
    · intro f p _; funext a; exact dist_subsingleton _ _
    · exact separates_of_spans h

/-! ## 6. How many probes?  Exactly `|α|` -/

/-- The `|α|` Dirac probes span. -/
theorem diracProbes_spans [DecidableEq α] : Spans (Set.range (dirac : α → Dist α)) := by
  rw [Spans, eq_top_iff]
  intro v _
  have hv : v = ∑ a, v a • (dirac a).p := by
    funext b
    simp only [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, dirac]
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single b] <;> simp +contextual [eq_comm]
  rw [hv]
  exact Submodule.sum_mem _ fun a _ =>
    Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨dirac a, ⟨a, rfl⟩, rfl⟩)

/-- **Lower bound on probe budgets.**  A spanning family of probe states has at
least `|α|` members: no budget certified on fewer probes than states can see
every channel. -/
theorem card_le_of_spans {m : ℕ} (probes : Fin m → Dist α)
    (h : Spans (Set.range probes)) : Fintype.card α ≤ m := by
  have hrange : Dist.p '' Set.range probes = Set.range (fun i => (probes i).p) := by
    rw [← Set.range_comp]; rfl
  have h1 := finrank_range_le_card (R := ℚ) (fun i => (probes i).p)
  rw [Set.finrank, ← hrange] at h1
  change Module.finrank ℚ (probeSpan (Set.range probes)) ≤ _ at h1
  rw [h, finrank_top, Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card] at h1
  simpa using h1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Necessity of Uniform Per-Layer Budgets -- numerical companion.

Everything is exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction), so every
equality printed below is an identity, not a floating-point coincidence.

Setting
-------
* A finite state space {0, ..., k-1}.
* A *law* is a probability vector of length k.
* A *channel* (layer) K is a row-stochastic k x k matrix: row a is the law K(a).
* push(K, mu) = mu K  (run one layer on an input law).
* A *stack* is a list of channels applied left to right.
* tv(mu, nu) = (1/2) * sum_b |mu_b - nu_b|  (total variation distance).

Sections
--------
 1. Soundness  <=>  uniform domination      (depth-additivity and its converse)
 2. Single-state certificates fail          (blind pairs for any non-spanning probe set)
 3. The probe-budget dichotomy              (spanning probe sets, probe count >= k)
 4. Masking suffixes                        (every pruning hides from solo probing)
 5. Trajectory costs and window extrapolation
 6. Design budgets and their amplification

Run:  python3 demo.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import random
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

Law = List[Fraction]
Channel = List[Law]          # row a = law K(a)
Stack = List[Channel]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic objects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def dirac(k: int, a: int) -> Law:
    """Point mass at state a."""
    return [Fraction(1) if b == a else Fraction(0) for b in range(k)]


def bern(t: Fraction) -> Law:
    """Two-state law putting mass t on state 1."""
    return [1 - t, t]


def push(K: Channel, mu: Sequence[Fraction]) -> Law:
    """Push a law (or any signed vector) through a channel: (mu K)_b = sum_a mu_a K(a)_b."""
    k = len(K)
    return [sum((mu[a] * K[a][b] for a in range(k)), Fraction(0)) for b in range(k)]


def chain(L: Stack, mu: Law) -> Law:
    """Run a whole stack on an input law."""
    for K in L:
        mu = push(K, mu)
    return mu


def tv(mu: Sequence[Fraction], nu: Sequence[Fraction]) -> Fraction:
    """Total variation distance (half the l1 distance)."""
    return sum((abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(mu, nu)), Fraction(0)) / 2


def identity(k: int) -> Channel:
    return [dirac(k, a) for a in range(k)]


def const_channel(d: Law) -> Channel:
    """The forgetful layer: every upstream state is sent to the law d."""
    return [list(d) for _ in range(len(d))]


def random_law(k: int, rng: random.Random, denom: int = 12) -> Law:
    w = [rng.randint(0, denom) for _ in range(k)]
    if sum(w) == 0:
        w[rng.randrange(k)] = 1
    s = sum(w)
    return [Fraction(x, s) for x in w]


def random_channel(k: int, rng: random.Random) -> Channel:
    return [random_law(k, rng) for _ in range(k)]


def perturb_channel(K: Channel, rng: random.Random, strength: Fraction) -> Channel:
    """Mix each row of K with a random law: a 'pruned' version of the layer."""
    k = len(K)
    out: Channel = []
    for row in K:
        r = random_law(k, rng)
        lam = strength * Fraction(rng.randint(0, 10), 10)
        out.append([(1 - lam) * x + lam * y for x, y in zip(row, r)])
    return out


def fmt(x: Fraction) -> str:
    return str(x) if x.denominator <= 1000 else f"{float(x):.6f}"


def fmt_law(mu: Sequence[Fraction]) -> str:
    return "(" + ", ".join(fmt(x) for x in mu) + ")"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Budgets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def uniform_budget(f: Channel, p: Channel) -> Fraction:
    """Worst case over upstream states of the per-layer perturbation."""
    return max(tv(f[a], p[a]) for a in range(len(f)))


def single_state_budget(f: Channel, p: Channel, s: Law) -> Fraction:
    """A budget certified only at one probe law s."""
    return tv(push(f, s), push(p, s))


def budget_sum(budget, F: Stack, P: Stack) -> Fraction:
    return sum((budget(f, p) for f, p in zip(F, P)), Fraction(0))


def hybrid_cost(F: Stack, P: Stack, mu: Law) -> Fraction:
    """Per-layer perturbations measured along the *pruned* trajectory."""
    total = Fraction(0)
    for f, p in zip(F, P):
        total += tv(push(f, mu), push(p, mu))
        mu = push(p, mu)
    return total


def trajectory_cost(F: Stack, P: Stack, mu: Law) -> Fraction:
    """Per-layer perturbations measured along the *intact* trajectory."""
    total = Fraction(0)
    for f, p in zip(F, P):
        total += tv(push(f, mu), push(p, mu))
        mu = push(f, mu)
    return total


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exact linear algebra over Q
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def rank(rows: List[Law]) -> int:
    M = [list(r) for r in rows]
    if not M:
        return 0
    n_cols = len(M[0])
    r = 0
    for c in range(n_cols):
        piv = next((i for i in range(r, len(M)) if M[i][c] != 0), None)
        if piv is None:
            continue
        M[r], M[piv] = M[piv], M[r]
        for i in range(len(M)):
            if i != r and M[i][c] != 0:
                fac = M[i][c] / M[r][c]
                M[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(M[i], M[r])]
        r += 1
    return r


def annihilator(rows: List[Law], k: int) -> Optional[Law]:
    """A nonzero w with sum_a s_a w_a = 0 for every row s, or None if the rows span Q^k."""
    M = [list(r) for r in rows]
    pivots: List[int] = []
    r = 0
    for c in range(k):
        piv = next((i for i in range(r, len(M)) if M[i][c] != 0), None)
        if piv is None:
            continue
        M[r], M[piv] = M[piv], M[r]
        lead = M[r][c]
        M[r] = [x / lead for x in M[r]]
        for i in range(len(M)):
            if i != r and M[i][c] != 0:
                fac = M[i][c]
                M[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(M[i], M[r])]
        pivots.append(c)
        r += 1
    free = [c for c in range(k) if c not in pivots]
    if not free:
        return None
    fc = free[0]
    w = [Fraction(0)] * k
    w[fc] = Fraction(1)
    for i, pc in enumerate(pivots):
        w[pc] = -M[i][fc]
    return w


def solve_dirac_coefficients(probes: List[Law]) -> List[List[Fraction]]:
    """For k linearly independent probes, return c with dirac(a) = sum_i c[a][i] probes[i]."""
    k = len(probes)
    # Solve c S = I where S has the probes as rows: c = S^{-1}.
    A = [list(probes[i]) + dirac(k, i) for i in range(k)]   # augment [S | I], invert S
    for c in range(k):
        piv = next(i for i in range(c, k) if A[i][c] != 0)
        A[c], A[piv] = A[piv], A[c]
        lead = A[c][c]
        A[c] = [x / lead for x in A[c]]
        for i in range(k):
            if i != c and A[i][c] != 0:
                fac = A[i][c]
                A[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(A[i], A[c])]
    Sinv = [row[k:] for row in A]
    return Sinv  # row a of S^{-1} expresses dirac(a)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm: witness interpolation (the blind pair)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def blind_pair(probes: List[Law], k: int, x: int = 0, y: int = 1
               ) -> Optional[Tuple[Channel, Channel, int]]:
    """
    If the probe vectors do not span Q^k (and k >= 2), build two channels g, q that
    respond identically to every probe but whose outputs at some state a0 are
    mutually singular (tv = 1).  Returns (g, q, a0) or None if the probes span.
    """
    w = annihilator(probes, k)
    if w is None:
        return None
    a0 = max(range(k), key=lambda a: abs(w[a]))
    M = abs(w[a0])
    u = [wa / M for wa in w]                 # |u_a| <= 1, |u_{a0}| = 1
    dx, dy = dirac(k, x), dirac(k, y)
    g = [[(1 + u[a]) / 2 * dx[b] + (1 - u[a]) / 2 * dy[b] for b in range(k)] for a in range(k)]
    q = [[(1 - u[a]) / 2 * dx[b] + (1 + u[a]) / 2 * dy[b] for b in range(k)] for a in range(k)]
    return g, q, a0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm: masking suffix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def mask_stacks(F: Stack, P: Stack, d: Law) -> Tuple[Stack, Stack]:
    """Collapse to d, run the original stack, then forget (intact) / pass through (pruned)."""
    k = len(d)
    Fm = [const_channel(d)] + F + [const_channel(chain(F, d))]
    Pm = [const_channel(d)] + P + [identity(k)]
    return Fm, Pm


def solo_cost(F: Stack, P: Stack, mu: Law, j: int) -> Fraction:
    """Output-level damage of ablating layer j alone (replace F[j] by P[j])."""
    G = list(F)
    G[j] = P[j]
    return tv(chain(F, mu), chain(G, mu))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Design budget
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def design_budget(probes: List[Law], coeffs: List[List[Fraction]], f: Channel, p: Channel
                  ) -> Fraction:
    """sum_a sum_i |c[a][i]| * tv(push f s_i, push p s_i): computed from probe responses only."""
    resp = [tv(push(f, s), push(p, s)) for s in probes]
    return sum((abs(coeffs[a][i]) * resp[i]
                for a in range(len(coeffs)) for i in range(len(probes))), Fraction(0))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sections
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def section_1(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("1. Soundness <=> uniform domination (depth-additivity)")
    k = 3
    worst_ratio = Fraction(0)
    for trial in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 6)
        F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 3)) for f in F]
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        joint = tv(chain(F, mu), chain(P, mu))
        hyb = hybrid_cost(F, P, mu)
        ub = budget_sum(uniform_budget, F, P)
        assert joint <= hyb <= ub, "depth-additivity violated?!"
        if ub > 0:
            worst_ratio = max(worst_ratio, joint / ub)
    print("200 random stack pairs on 3 states, depths 1..6:")
    print("  joint damage <= hybrid cost <= sum of uniform budgets  held in every case.")
    print(f"  largest observed ratio joint / (sum of uniform budgets) = {fmt(worst_ratio)}")

    # Closed form n * eps
    eps = Fraction(1, 20)
    f = identity(2)
    p = [[1 - eps, eps], [eps, 1 - eps]]       # flips with probability eps
    for n in (1, 2, 5, 10):
        F, P = [f] * n, [p] * n
        joint = tv(chain(F, dirac(2, 0)), chain(P, dirac(2, 0)))
        print(f"  depth {n:2d}, each layer eps = 1/20 in the worst case: joint = {fmt(joint):>10}"
              f"  <= n*eps = {fmt(n * eps)}")

    # Necessity: the uniform budget is the least sound budget.
    f, p = random_channel(3, rng), random_channel(3, rng)
    a_star = max(range(3), key=lambda a: tv(f[a], p[a]))
    print(f"  Necessity: depth-one stack fed the Dirac input at state {a_star} has damage"
          f" {fmt(tv(f[a_star], p[a_star]))} = uniform budget {fmt(uniform_budget(f, p))}.")
    print("  So any budget charging less than the worst case is unsound on that one-layer stack.")


def section_2() -> None:
    banner("2. Single-state certificates fail: the blind pair")
    # The balanced probe on two states cannot tell identity from a flip.
    s = bern(Fraction(1, 2))
    idk = identity(2)
    flip = [dirac(2, 1), dirac(2, 0)]
    print(f"Probe s = {fmt_law(s)}.  push(id, s) = {fmt_law(push(idk, s))},"
          f" push(flip, s) = {fmt_law(push(flip, s))}")
    print(f"  but tv(id(0), flip(0)) = {fmt(tv(idk[0], flip[0]))}: a single-state budget charges 0,"
          " the damage at the Dirac input is 1.")

    # Witness interpolation through an arbitrary non-spanning probe set on 4 states.
    k = 4
    probes = [[Fraction(1, 4)] * 4,
              [Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6)],
              [Fraction(1, 10), Fraction(2, 10), Fraction(3, 10), Fraction(4, 10)]]
    print(f"\nNon-spanning probe set on {k} states (rank {rank(probes)} < {k}):")
    for pr in probes:
        print("   ", fmt_law(pr))
    res = blind_pair(probes, k)
    assert res is not None
    g, q, a0 = res
    for i, pr in enumerate(probes):
        rg, rq = push(g, pr), push(q, pr)
        assert rg == rq
        print(f"  probe {i}: g responds {fmt_law(rg)}, q responds {fmt_law(rq)}  (identical)")
    print(f"  but at state a0 = {a0}: g(a0) = {fmt_law(g[a0])}, q(a0) = {fmt_law(q[a0])},"
          f" tv = {fmt(tv(g[a0], q[a0]))}")

    # Any probe-blind budget: total budget 0 at every depth, damage 1.
    for n in (0, 3, 7):
        F = [g] + [identity(k)] * n
        P = [q] + [identity(k)] * n
        dmg = tv(chain(F, dirac(k, a0)), chain(P, dirac(k, a0)))
        print(f"  depth {n + 1}: every calibrated probe-local budget totals 0, joint damage = {fmt(dmg)}")


def section_3() -> None:
    banner("3. The probe-budget dichotomy: spanning is necessary and sufficient")
    k = 3
    families = {
        "one interior probe": [[Fraction(1, 3)] * 3],
        "two probes": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
                       [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)]],
        "three interior probes": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
                                  [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)],
                                  [Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(2, 3)]],
        "three probes, dependent": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0)],
                                    [Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2)],
                                    [Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4)]],
        "the 3 Dirac probes": [dirac(3, a) for a in range(3)],
    }
    for name, probes in families.items():
        r = rank(probes)
        verdict = "SPANS  -> a sound calibrated probe-local budget exists" if r == k else \
            "fails  -> every calibrated probe-local budget is unsound"
        print(f"  {name:26s} rank {r}/{k}: {verdict}")
        if r < k:
            res = blind_pair(probes, k)
            assert res is not None
            g, q, a0 = res
            assert all(push(g, s) == push(q, s) for s in probes)
            assert tv(g[a0], q[a0]) == 1
    print("  Note the dependent family: three probes are not enough unless they are independent;")
    print("  fewer than k = 3 probes never suffice.")


def section_4(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("4. Masking suffix: every pruning instance hides from solo probing")
    k = 3
    F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(3)]
    P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1)) for f in F]
    d = random_law(k, rng)
    original = tv(chain(F, d), chain(P, d))
    Fm, Pm = mask_stacks(F, P, d)
    print(f"Original depth-3 pair, probe state d = {fmt_law(d)}: joint damage at d = {fmt(original)}")
    print("  original solo costs at d:",
          ", ".join(fmt(solo_cost(F, P, d, j)) for j in range(3)))
    for trial in range(3):
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        joint = tv(chain(Fm, mu), chain(Pm, mu))
        solos = [solo_cost(Fm, Pm, mu, j) for j in range(len(Fm))]
        assert joint == original and all(sc == 0 for sc in solos)
        print(f"  masked (depth 5) at input {fmt_law(mu)}: joint = {fmt(joint)},"
              f" solo costs = {[fmt(sc) for sc in solos]}")

    # The NET-59 numbers: two states, probe d0, target 17/1000.
    t = Fraction(17, 1000)
    d0 = dirac(2, 0)
    n = 2
    F = [identity(2)] * (n + 1)
    P = [const_channel(bern(t))] * (n + 1)
    Fm, Pm = mask_stacks(F, P, d0)
    mu = bern(Fraction(2, 3))
    print(f"\n  Witness family on 2 states, depth {len(Fm)}: joint damage at {fmt_law(mu)} ="
          f" {fmt(tv(chain(Fm, mu), chain(Pm, mu)))}, solo profile ="
          f" {[fmt(solo_cost(Fm, Pm, mu, j)) for j in range(len(Fm))]}")


def section_5(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("5. Trajectory costs: sound on the window, extrapolate only through the span")
    k = 3
    viol = 0
    for _ in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 2)) for f in F]
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        if tv(chain(F, mu), chain(P, mu)) > trajectory_cost(F, P, mu):
            viol += 1
    print(f"  200 random pairs: joint damage <= intact-trajectory cost violated {viol} times.")

    # Window extrapolation on two states, window {bern 1/4, bern 3/4}.
    w1, w2 = bern(Fraction(1, 4)), bern(Fraction(3, 4))
    c = [Fraction(3, 2), Fraction(-1, 2)]
    comb = [c[0] * w1[b] + c[1] * w2[b] for b in range(2)]
    print(f"  d0 = 3/2 * bern(1/4) - 1/2 * bern(3/4) = {fmt_law(comb)}   (l1 amplification 2)")
    worst = Fraction(0)
    for _ in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        F = [random_channel(2, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 2)) for f in F]
        lhs = tv(chain(F, dirac(2, 0)), chain(P, dirac(2, 0)))
        rhs = abs(c[0]) * trajectory_cost(F, P, w1) + abs(c[1]) * trajectory_cost(F, P, w2)
        assert lhs <= rhs
        if rhs > 0:
            worst = max(worst, lhs / rhs)
    print(f"  extrapolated bound held on 200 random pairs; tightest ratio = {fmt(worst)}")


def section_6(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("6. Design budgets: an explicit sound budget from probe measurements")
    probes = [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
              [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)],
              [Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(2, 3)]]
    C = solve_dirac_coefficients(probes)
    for a in range(3):
        recon = [sum((C[a][i] * probes[i][b] for i in range(3)), Fraction(0)) for b in range(3)]
        assert recon == dirac(3, a)
        print(f"  dirac({a}) = " + " + ".join(f"({fmt(C[a][i])})*s{i}" for i in range(3))
              + f"   amplification {fmt(sum(abs(x) for x in C[a]))}")
    for _ in range(300):
        f = random_channel(3, rng)
        p = perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1))
        assert design_budget(probes, C, f, p) >= uniform_budget(f, p)
    print("  design budget >= uniform budget on 300 random layer pairs  (hence sound).")

    print("\n  Amplification of the symmetric two-state design {bern(eta), bern(1-eta)}:")
    for eta in (Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 10), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(2, 5), Fraction(9, 20)):
        Cd = solve_dirac_coefficients([bern(eta), bern(1 - eta)])
        amp = max(sum(abs(x) for x in row) for row in Cd)
        print(f"    eta = {fmt(eta):>5}: max_a sum_i |c_ai| = {fmt(amp):>4}   (1/(1-2 eta) = {fmt(1 / (1 - 2 * eta))})")


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(59)
    section_1(rng)
    section_2()
    section_3()
    section_4(rng)
    section_5(rng)
    section_6(rng)
    print("\nAll checks passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Computational evidence: probe-local per-layer budgets

Model: the setting of `Probability.NET59TVCore` and `Probability.NET59HybridEpistasis`. Layers are Markov channels on a finite state space with rational weights, and damage is total variation distance. Every number below is stated and checked by a Lean declaration in `Catalog/Applications/NET59ProbeBudgets/`. None of it comes from an unchecked script.

## 1. Small cases

| State space | Probe set | Spans? | What Lean verifies | Declaration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Fin 2` | `{bern 1/2}` (one balanced held-out input) | no | `idK` and `flipK` give identical responses at the probe, but `tv(idK 0, flipK 0) = 1` | `ProbeDesign.lean`, LabNotes, first `example` |
| `Fin 2` | `{bern 1/4, bern 3/4}` | yes | `d0 = 3/2·bern 1/4 − 1/2·bern 3/4` | `lab_d0_combination` |
| `Fin 2` | same | yes | joint damage from `d0` ≤ `3/2·traj(bern 1/4) + 1/2·traj(bern 3/4)` for every stack pair (ℓ¹ amplification 2) | LabNotes, second `example` |
| `Fin 2`, any depth `n+3` | any inputs at all | n/a | masked witness: solo profile `0` at every input and every layer; joint damage `17/1000` at every input | `MaskingSuffix.lean`, LabNotes `example` |
| any `α`, `m < |α|` probes | `Fin m → Dist α` | never | a stack pair that agrees exactly on the window but has damage `1` elsewhere | `small_window_never_certifies` |

## 2. OEIS

Not applicable. No integer sequence comes up. The only count in the results is the minimum number of probes, which is exactly `|α|` (`diracProbes_spans`, `card_le_of_spans`).

## 3. Counterexample hunt

The original conjecture says that every finitely-probed budget fails. That conjecture is false as stated, and the Lean results show why:

* If the state space is finite, the `|α|` Dirac probes span. The Dirac-sum and design budgets are probe-local, calibrated and sound (`diracProbes_suffice`, `designBudget_sound`). So some finitely-probed budgets succeed.
* On a one-point state space every budget that vanishes on equal layers is sound. This corner case is the reason the `Subsingleton α` disjunct appears in `probe_budget_dichotomy`.
* The correct statement is the dichotomy. A sound, calibrated, probe-local budget exists **iff** the probes span (or `|α| = 1`).

A further corner case appeared during formalization. With `m = 0` probes on a one-point space we have `m < |α|`, yet no damage is possible. For this reason `small_window_never_certifies` assumes `Nontrivial α`.

## 4. Table: what each kind of measurement certifies

| Measurement | Sound for the measured input? | Sound for all inputs? |
|---|---|---|
| uniform worst-case per layer | yes | yes (`budget_sound_iff_uniform_le`) |
| layer-output perturbation on the input's own intact trajectory | yes (`joint_le_trajectoryCost`) | iff the window spans (`trajectory_window_dichotomy`) |
| per-layer response at fixed probe states | n/a | iff the probes span (`probe_budget_dichotomy`) |
| output-level solo ablation | **no** (`masking_suffix`, `solo_certificate_unsound`) | no |

# Summary of changes for run addd699a-19d5-485f-bceb-b3441b367375
I wrote the five Phase B files, published them, and committed them to the repository. None of them adds or changes any proofs. I did not re-check the existing proof files: one module they import is missing from this project, so they can't be built here. A search found no `sorry` in them.

**What the documents cover.** All three prose documents leave out proof tooling, file paths and code identifiers, and state every result in ordinary mathematical language:
- A per-layer budget is sound exactly when it is at least each layer's worst-case perturbation over upstream states. So the worst-case ("uniform") budget is the smallest sound budget, and \(n\) layers that are each \(\varepsilon\)-close do at most \(n\varepsilon\) damage.
- Probe-budget dichotomy: a sound budget that sees layers only through a set of probe inputs, and charges nothing for an unchanged layer, exists if and only if the probes span the state space. So at least \(k\) probes are needed for \(k\) states.
- If the probes don't span, a construction gives, at every depth, two stacks with total budget 0 and damage 1, and no slack term repairs this. Held-out windows with fewer inputs than states never certify agreement.
- Masking suffix: adding two layers hides any pruning from every one-layer-at-a-time ablation, at every input, without changing the joint damage.
- Positive side: measurements along an input's own intact trajectory are sound for that input. They extend to other inputs at a cost equal to the \(\ell^1\) norm of the combination coefficients, which gives a sound budget built from probe measurements alone.

The paper also points out that the original conjecture is false for spanning probe sets and needs the "charges nothing for an unchanged layer" condition. It lists the three Phase A conjectures as open problems.

**The files:**
- `ARTICLE.md`: a popular-science article of about 2,400 words.
- `RESEARCH_PAPER.md`: the research paper, about 5,800 words, with abstract, definitions, theorems with proof sketches, three algorithms, applications, discussion and future work.
- `RESEARCH_PAPER.tex`: a LaTeX (amsart) version of the paper. No LaTeX compiler was available, so it has not been compiled. I only checked that the `begin`/`end` environments, braces and math delimiters are balanced.
- `demo.py`: standard-library Python using exact fractions. It runs cleanly and checks every result above on random examples, including the two-state example with damage \(17/1000\) and the window example \(\delta_0=\tfrac32\beta_{1/4}-\tfrac12\beta_{3/4}\). These are numerical checks, not proofs.
- `PACKAGE.json`: contains the full text of all of the above plus:
  - **Algorithms:** three, each with pseudocode and runnable Python: the blind-pair construction, the probe-based design budget, and the masking suffix.
  - **Visualizations:** two matplotlib scripts. matplotlib isn't installed here, so I could only run their numerical parts.
  - **Interactive widgets:** two HTML pages. One is a three-state "Probe Lab" where you drag probes and see either the blind pair or the design coefficients. The other is a masking-suffix explorer. I tested their logic with a stand-in for the browser, not in a real browser.
  - **Guided-tour page:** a step-by-step page that places all of these inline and hides the proofs in expandable sections.
  - **Future directions:** the Phase A text, lightly edited to replace code names with theorem names and to finish its cut-off last sentence.

# Future directions: probe-local per-layer budgets

This cycle established the following, all in `Catalog/Applications/NET59ProbeBudgets/`:

* A per-layer budget is sound **iff** it dominates the worst-case perturbation over states (`budget_sound_iff_uniform_le`).
* A probe set supports a sound, calibrated, probe-local budget **iff** its probe vectors span `ℚ^α`, or `|α| = 1` (`probe_budget_dichotomy`). At least `|α|` probes are needed (`probe_count_lower_bound`).
* Every pruning instance can be hidden from output-level solo probing at every input by adding two layers (`masking_suffix`).
* Measurements taken along the input's own intact trajectory are sound for that input. They extrapolate to other inputs with amplification equal to the ℓ¹ norm of the coefficients that express those inputs in terms of the window (`window_extrapolation`, `designBudget_sound`).

The conjectures below build on these results.

## 1. Optimal amplification of interior probe designs

**Conjecture.** Let `|α| = k` and suppose every probe is an η-interior input, meaning each state has probability at least `η`, with `0 ≤ η < 1/k`. Take the smallest possible value, over spanning probe families and coefficient choices, of `max_a Σ_i |c a i|`. This value is exactly `(1 + (k−2)η)/(1 − kη)`. It is attained by the shrunk vertices `(1−kη)δ_a + η𝟙`.

The key insight is that the design budget's amplification is the ℓ¹ norm of the coefficients expressing the vertices of the simplex in terms of the probes. So the best design is a polytope-inscription problem in the simplex.

Why now? `designBudget_sound` turns any spanning probe family into an explicit sound budget. Deployment probes are always interior: real inputs are never Dirac masses. The constant in front of the budget is therefore the one quantity left to optimise.

## 2. Epistatic factor law along the pruned trajectory

**Conjecture.** For stacks of depth `n`, the hybrid cost along the pruned trajectory satisfies `hybridCost ≤ Σ_j (2(n−1−j)+1) · point_j`, where `point_j` is the perturbation on the intact trajectory. The odd factors `2(n−1−j)+1` are tight. Depth 2 gives the factor `3` already proved in `chain_bound_of_points`.

The key insight is that each upstream perturbation is paid once directly and then again, twice, through context shift at every downstream layer. The repeated use of `tv_push_context_shift` telescopes into odd weights.

Why now? `joint_le_trajectoryCost` showed that intact-trajectory costs bound the joint damage with factor `1`, while the hybrid bound needs the pruned trajectory. The gap between the two accountings is exactly this epistatic factor.

## 3. No finite probe set on infinite state spaces

**Conjecture.** For channels on an infinite standard Borel space, no finite set of probe laws supports a sound, calibrated, probe-local budget. More strongly, a probe set supports one iff its linear span is weak-* dense in the bounded signed measures.

The key insight is that `card_le_of_spans` is a dimension count. On an infinite space the dimension is infinite, so the finite-probe side of the dichotomy is empty.

Why now? Transformer state spaces are effectively continuous. The finite-`α` dichotomy proved here is the template, and Mathlib's measure-theory library can now express the needed signed-measure duality.

## 4. Random windows: span almost surely, heavy-tailed amplification

**Conjecture.** Draw `m ≥ k = |α|` window inputs i.i.d. from a Dirichlet(1,…,1) law. The window spans almost surely. The optimal ℓ¹ amplification `A_m` satisfies `E[log A_m] = Θ(log k)` for `m = k`. For `m ≥ 2k` it concentrates around a constant independent of `k`.

The key insight is that the amplification is governed by the smallest singular value of the random probe matrix. Random-matrix theory controls that value, and oversampling stabilises it.

Why now? `small_window_never_certifies` shows that `m < k` windows are hopeless. The live question for experimental design is how much oversampling beyond `k` makes held-out windows usable.

## 5. Masking depth is exactly two

**Conjecture.** Some pruning instances (for example, the identity intact stack with one constant pruned layer, on a nontrivial `α`) cannot be embedded in a stack only one layer deeper that has an identically zero solo profile at every input and the same joint damage. So the `+2` in `masking_suffix` is optimal.

The key insight is that masking needs two separate jobs: a collapsing prefix that makes the last layer's solo ablation see one fixed state, and a forgetful suffix that hides the inner layers. A single extra layer cannot do both.

Why now? `masking_suffix` gives the upper bound `2`. A matching lower bound would give a tight "price of invisibility" for solo-profile audits.
