def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def section_1(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("1. Soundness <=> uniform domination (depth-additivity)")
    k = 3
    worst_ratio = Fraction(0)
    for trial in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 6)
        F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 3)) for f in F]
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        joint = tv(chain(F, mu), chain(P, mu))
        hyb = hybrid_cost(F, P, mu)
        ub = budget_sum(uniform_budget, F, P)
        assert joint <= hyb <= ub, "depth-additivity violated?!"
        if ub > 0:
            worst_ratio = max(worst_ratio, joint / ub)
    print("200 random stack pairs on 3 states, depths 1..6:")
    print("  joint damage <= hybrid cost <= sum of uniform budgets  held in every case.")
    print(f"  largest observed ratio joint / (sum of uniform budgets) = {fmt(worst_ratio)}")

    # Closed form n * eps
    eps = Fraction(1, 20)
    f = identity(2)
    p = [[1 - eps, eps], [eps, 1 - eps]]       # flips with probability eps
    for n in (1, 2, 5, 10):
        F, P = [f] * n, [p] * n
        joint = tv(chain(F, dirac(2, 0)), chain(P, dirac(2, 0)))
        print(f"  depth {n:2d}, each layer eps = 1/20 in the worst case: joint = {fmt(joint):>10}"
              f"  <= n*eps = {fmt(n * eps)}")

    # Necessity: the uniform budget is the least sound budget.
    f, p = random_channel(3, rng), random_channel(3, rng)
    a_star = max(range(3), key=lambda a: tv(f[a], p[a]))
    print(f"  Necessity: depth-one stack fed the Dirac input at state {a_star} has damage"
          f" {fmt(tv(f[a_star], p[a_star]))} = uniform budget {fmt(uniform_budget(f, p))}.")
    print("  So any budget charging less than the worst case is unsound on that one-layer stack.")


def section_2() -> None:
    banner("2. Single-state certificates fail: the blind pair")
    # The balanced probe on two states cannot tell identity from a flip.
    s = bern(Fraction(1, 2))
    idk = identity(2)
    flip = [dirac(2, 1), dirac(2, 0)]
    print(f"Probe s = {fmt_law(s)}.  push(id, s) = {fmt_law(push(idk, s))},"
          f" push(flip, s) = {fmt_law(push(flip, s))}")
    print(f"  but tv(id(0), flip(0)) = {fmt(tv(idk[0], flip[0]))}: a single-state budget charges 0,"
          " the damage at the Dirac input is 1.")

    # Witness interpolation through an arbitrary non-spanning probe set on 4 states.
    k = 4
    probes = [[Fraction(1, 4)] * 4,
              [Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6)],
              [Fraction(1, 10), Fraction(2, 10), Fraction(3, 10), Fraction(4, 10)]]
    print(f"\nNon-spanning probe set on {k} states (rank {rank(probes)} < {k}):")
    for pr in probes:
        print("   ", fmt_law(pr))
    res = blind_pair(probes, k)
    assert res is not None
    g, q, a0 = res
    for i, pr in enumerate(probes):
        rg, rq = push(g, pr), push(q, pr)
        assert rg == rq
        print(f"  probe {i}: g responds {fmt_law(rg)}, q responds {fmt_law(rq)}  (identical)")
    print(f"  but at state a0 = {a0}: g(a0) = {fmt_law(g[a0])}, q(a0) = {fmt_law(q[a0])},"
          f" tv = {fmt(tv(g[a0], q[a0]))}")

    # Any probe-blind budget: total budget 0 at every depth, damage 1.
    for n in (0, 3, 7):
        F = [g] + [identity(k)] * n
        P = [q] + [identity(k)] * n
        dmg = tv(chain(F, dirac(k, a0)), chain(P, dirac(k, a0)))
        print(f"  depth {n + 1}: every calibrated probe-local budget totals 0, joint damage = {fmt(dmg)}")


def section_3() -> None:
    banner("3. The probe-budget dichotomy: spanning is necessary and sufficient")
    k = 3
    families = {
        "one interior probe": [[Fraction(1, 3)] * 3],
        "two probes": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
                       [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)]],
        "three interior probes": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
                                  [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)],
                                  [Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(2, 3)]],
        "three probes, dependent": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0)],
                                    [Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2)],
                                    [Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4)]],
        "the 3 Dirac probes": [dirac(3, a) for a in range(3)],
    }
    for name, probes in families.items():
        r = rank(probes)
        verdict = "SPANS  -> a sound calibrated probe-local budget exists" if r == k else \
            "fails  -> every calibrated probe-local budget is unsound"
        print(f"  {name:26s} rank {r}/{k}: {verdict}")
        if r < k:
            res = blind_pair(probes, k)
            assert res is not None
            g, q, a0 = res
            assert all(push(g, s) == push(q, s) for s in probes)
            assert tv(g[a0], q[a0]) == 1
    print("  Note the dependent family: three probes are not enough unless they are independent;")
    print("  fewer than k = 3 probes never suffice.")


def section_4(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("4. Masking suffix: every pruning instance hides from solo probing")
    k = 3
    F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(3)]
    P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1)) for f in F]
    d = random_law(k, rng)
    original = tv(chain(F, d), chain(P, d))
    Fm, Pm = mask_stacks(F, P, d)
    print(f"Original depth-3 pair, probe state d = {fmt_law(d)}: joint damage at d = {fmt(original)}")
    print("  original solo costs at d:",
          ", ".join(fmt(solo_cost(F, P, d, j)) for j in range(3)))
    for trial in range(3):
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        joint = tv(chain(Fm, mu), chain(Pm, mu))
        solos = [solo_cost(Fm, Pm, mu, j) for j in range(len(Fm))]
        assert joint == original and all(sc == 0 for sc in solos)
        print(f"  masked (depth 5) at input {fmt_law(mu)}: joint = {fmt(joint)},"
              f" solo costs = {[fmt(sc) for sc in solos]}")

    # The NET-59 numbers: two states, probe d0, target 17/1000.
    t = Fraction(17, 1000)
    d0 = dirac(2, 0)
    n = 2
    F = [identity(2)] * (n + 1)
    P = [const_channel(bern(t))] * (n + 1)
    Fm, Pm = mask_stacks(F, P, d0)
    mu = bern(Fraction(2, 3))
    print(f"\n  Witness family on 2 states, depth {len(Fm)}: joint damage at {fmt_law(mu)} ="
          f" {fmt(tv(chain(Fm, mu), chain(Pm, mu)))}, solo profile ="
          f" {[fmt(solo_cost(Fm, Pm, mu, j)) for j in range(len(Fm))]}")


def section_5(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("5. Trajectory costs: sound on the window, extrapolate only through the span")
    k = 3
    viol = 0
    for _ in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 2)) for f in F]
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        if tv(chain(F, mu), chain(P, mu)) > trajectory_cost(F, P, mu):
            viol += 1
    print(f"  200 random pairs: joint damage <= intact-trajectory cost violated {viol} times.")

    # Window extrapolation on two states, window {bern 1/4, bern 3/4}.
    w1, w2 = bern(Fraction(1, 4)), bern(Fraction(3, 4))
    c = [Fraction(3, 2), Fraction(-1, 2)]
    comb = [c[0] * w1[b] + c[1] * w2[b] for b in range(2)]
    print(f"  d0 = 3/2 * bern(1/4) - 1/2 * bern(3/4) = {fmt_law(comb)}   (l1 amplification 2)")
    worst = Fraction(0)
    for _ in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        F = [random_channel(2, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 2)) for f in F]
        lhs = tv(chain(F, dirac(2, 0)), chain(P, dirac(2, 0)))
        rhs = abs(c[0]) * trajectory_cost(F, P, w1) + abs(c[1]) * trajectory_cost(F, P, w2)
        assert lhs <= rhs
        if rhs > 0:
            worst = max(worst, lhs / rhs)
    print(f"  extrapolated bound held on 200 random pairs; tightest ratio = {fmt(worst)}")


def section_6(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("6. Design budgets: an explicit sound budget from probe measurements")
    probes = [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
              [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)],
              [Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(2, 3)]]
    C = solve_dirac_coefficients(probes)
    for a in range(3):
        recon = [sum((C[a][i] * probes[i][b] for i in range(3)), Fraction(0)) for b in range(3)]
        assert recon == dirac(3, a)
        print(f"  dirac({a}) = " + " + ".join(f"({fmt(C[a][i])})*s{i}" for i in range(3))
              + f"   amplification {fmt(sum(abs(x) for x in C[a]))}")
    for _ in range(300):
        f = random_channel(3, rng)
        p = perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1))
        assert design_budget(probes, C, f, p) >= uniform_budget(f, p)
    print("  design budget >= uniform budget on 300 random layer pairs  (hence sound).")

    print("\n  Amplification of the symmetric two-state design {bern(eta), bern(1-eta)}:")
    for eta in (Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 10), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(2, 5), Fraction(9, 20)):
        Cd = solve_dirac_coefficients([bern(eta), bern(1 - eta)])
        amp = max(sum(abs(x) for x in row) for row in Cd)
        print(f"    eta = {fmt(eta):>5}: max_a sum_i |c_ai| = {fmt(amp):>4}   (1/(1-2 eta) = {fmt(1 / (1 - 2 * eta))})")


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(59)
    section_1(rng)
    section_2()
    section_3()
    section_4(rng)
    section_5(rng)
    section_6(rng)
    print("\nAll checks passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple

Law = List[Fraction]
Channel = List[Law]


def null_vector(probes: List[Law], k: int) -> Optional[Law]:
    """Return w != 0 with sum_a s_a w_a = 0 for every probe s, or None if the probes span Q^k."""
    M = [list(r) for r in probes]
    pivots: List[int] = []
    r = 0
    for c in range(k):
        piv = next((i for i in range(r, len(M)) if M[i][c] != 0), None)
        if piv is None:
            continue
        M[r], M[piv] = M[piv], M[r]
        lead = M[r][c]
        M[r] = [x / lead for x in M[r]]
        for i in range(len(M)):
            if i != r and M[i][c] != 0:
                fac = M[i][c]
                M[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(M[i], M[r])]
        pivots.append(c)
        r += 1
    free = [c for c in range(k) if c not in pivots]
    if not free:
        return None
    w = [Fraction(0)] * k
    w[free[0]] = Fraction(1)
    for i, pc in enumerate(pivots):
        w[pc] = -M[i][free[0]]
    return w


def blind_pair(probes: List[Law], k: int, x: int = 0, y: int = 1
               ) -> Optional[Tuple[Channel, Channel, int]]:
    """Channels g, q with identical responses at every probe and tv(g(a0), q(a0)) = 1."""
    w = null_vector(probes, k)
    if w is None:
        return None
    a0 = max(range(k), key=lambda a: abs(w[a]))
    u = [wa / abs(w[a0]) for wa in w]
    def row(a: int, sign: int) -> Law:
        r = [Fraction(0)] * k
        r[x] += (1 + sign * u[a]) / 2
        r[y] += (1 - sign * u[a]) / 2
        return r
    g = [row(a, +1) for a in range(k)]
    q = [row(a, -1) for a in range(k)]
    return g, q, a0

from typing import List

def invert(S: List[Law]) -> List[List[Fraction]]:
    """Gauss-Jordan inverse over Q. Row a of the result expresses delta_a in terms of the rows of S."""
    k = len(S)

        piv = next(i for i in range(c, k) if A[i][c] != 0)   # raises if the probes do not span

        lead = A[c][c]
        A[c] = [x / lead for x in A[c]]
        for i in range(k):

                A[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(A[i], A[c])]

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, Tuple

Law = List[Fraction]
Channel = List[Law]
Stack = List[Channel]


def push(K: Channel, mu: Law) -> Law:
    return [sum((mu[a] * K[a][b] for a in range(len(K))), Fraction(0)) for b in range(len(K))]

def const(d: Law) -> Channel:
    return [list(d) for _ in d]


def identity(k: int) -> Channel:
    return [[Fraction(int(a == b)) for b in range(k)] for a in range(k)]


def mask(F: Stack, P: Stack, d: Law) -> Tuple[Stack, Stack]:
    """Collapsing prefix kappa_d; forgetful suffix kappa_{F(d)} (intact) / identity (pruned)."""
    return [const(d)] + F + [const(run(F, d))], [const(d)] + P + [identity(len(d))]


def solo(F: Stack, P: Stack, mu: Law, j: int) -> Fraction:
    G = list(F)
    G[j] = P[j]
    return tv(run(F, mu), run(G, mu))

## 1. The accounting we would like to do

You compress a deep model layer by layer. For each layer you measure how much its output moved, add the numbers up, and report the sum as a bound on how much the whole model changed. Is the sum really a bound?

We model each layer as a **channel**: a [Markov kernel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_kernel) on a finite set of $k$ internal states. A layer sends state $a$ to a random state with law $f(a)$. A network is a **stack** of channels, and differences between output laws are measured by the [total variation distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_variation_distance_of_probability_measures)
$$\operatorname{tv}(\mu,\nu)=\tfrac12\sum_b|\mu_b-\nu_b|\in[0,1].$$

<details><summary><b>Background: laws, channels and stacks in symbols</b></summary>

* A *law* is a probability vector $\mu\in\mathbb{Q}^k$. The point mass at state $a$ is $\delta_a$.
* A channel $K$ is a row-stochastic matrix. Its rows are the laws $K(a)$, and it acts on laws by $(\mu K)_b=\sum_a\mu_aK(a)_b$.
* A stack $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ maps $\mu\mapsto F(\mu)=\mu f_1\cdots f_n$.
* For an intact stack $F$ and a pruned stack $P$ of the same depth, the **joint damage** from input $\mu$ is $\operatorname{tv}(F(\mu),P(\mu))$.
* Channels are *linear* in the input law, and the composite of a stack is again a channel, $\widehat F(a)=F(\delta_a)$.
</details>

A **per-layer budget functional** is any rule $B(f,p)$ assigning a number to each (intact, pruned) layer pair. It is **sound** if
$$\operatorname{tv}(F(\mu),P(\mu))\le\sum_j B(f_j,p_j)$$
for every pair of stacks of equal depth and every input law $\mu$.

## 2. Soundness means worst-case, exactly

> **Theorem 1 (soundness is uniform domination).** $B$ is sound if and only if $B(f,p)\ge\operatorname{tv}(f(a),p(a))$ for every layer pair and every state $a$. Equivalently, $B$ dominates the **uniform budget** $U(f,p)=\max_a\operatorname{tv}(f(a),p(a))$, which is itself sound and is therefore the least sound budget.

<details><summary>Click to reveal the proof</summary>

**Necessity.** Feed the one-layer stacks $(f)$ and $(p)$ the point mass $\delta_a$. The damage is $\operatorname{tv}(f(a),p(a))$, and the budget is $B(f,p)$.

**Sufficiency.** The [hybrid argument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_argument_(Cryptography)) bounds the damage by $\sum_j\operatorname{tv}(\nu_jf_j,\nu_jp_j)$, where $\nu_j=\mu p_1\cdots p_{j-1}$ is the law produced by the *pruned* prefix. Each term is at most $\max_a\operatorname{tv}(f_j(a),p_j(a))$, because $\nu_jf_j-\nu_jp_j=\sum_a(\nu_j)_a(f_j(a)-p_j(a))$ is an average of the per-state differences.
</details>

In particular, $n$ layers that are each $\varepsilon$-close in the worst case do at most $n\varepsilon$ damage. The visualization below shows this depth-additivity on random stacks, and contrasts it with budgets certified at a single state.

## 3. Probes: when can a few inputs certify a layer?

The worst case ranges over $k$ states. Perhaps measuring a layer at a few well-chosen **probe** laws is enough? We ask for budgets that are

* **probe-local**: they depend on a layer pair only through its responses $sf, sp$ at the probes $s\in S$;
* **calibrated**: an unchanged layer is charged $0$. Without this, the constant budget $B\equiv1$ would be trivially sound.

> **Theorem 2 (probe-budget dichotomy).** A sound, calibrated, probe-local budget exists **if and only if** the probe vectors [span](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_span) $\mathbb{Q}^k$, or $k=1$. Hence at least $k$ probes are required, and the $k$ point masses suffice.

With three states, every law is a point in a triangle, and three probes span exactly when they do not lie on one line. Try it below. Drag the probes, collapse them onto a line, or reduce their number, and watch the **witness interpolation** construction produce two layers that agree at every probe yet disagree completely at one state.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

<details><summary>Click to reveal the witness-interpolation construction</summary>

If the probes do not span, pick $w\neq0$ with $\sum_as_aw_a=0$ for every probe $s$. Let $a_0$ maximise $|w_a|$, and set $u=w/|w_{a_0}|$, so that $|u_a|\le1$ and $|u_{a_0}|=1$. Fix two states $x\ne y$ and define
$$g(a)=\tfrac{1+u_a}2\delta_x+\tfrac{1-u_a}2\delta_y,\qquad q(a)=\tfrac{1-u_a}2\delta_x+\tfrac{1+u_a}2\delta_y.$$
At every probe, both responses equal $\tfrac12\delta_x+\tfrac12\delta_y$. At $a_0$, the outputs are $\delta_x$ and $\delta_y$, at distance $1$. Pad with identity layers to obtain, at **every depth**, a stack pair with total budget $0$ and damage $1$. No relaxation "damage $\le C\cdot$budget$+\delta$" with $\delta<1$ survives.
</details>

### Held-out windows

The same linear algebra governs held-out evaluation. Agreement of two stacks on every input of a window certifies agreement everywhere **iff the window spans**. A window with fewer inputs than states never certifies anything: some pair agrees exactly on the window and differs maximally elsewhere.

## 4. The masking suffix: solo ablations can be blind everywhere

What if we ablate layers *in context*? Replace one layer at a time by its pruned version, run the whole network, and look at the output, at as many inputs as we like.

> **Theorem 3 (masking suffix).** For any stacks $F,P$ and any law $d$, let $\widetilde F=(\kappa_d,F,\kappa_{F(d)})$ and $\widetilde P=(\kappa_d,P,\mathrm{id})$, where $\kappa_c$ is the constant layer that always outputs $c$. Then from **every** input the joint damage equals $\operatorname{tv}(F(d),P(d))$, and **every** single-layer ablation leaves the output unchanged.

Switch the suffix on and off below, and sweep the input law.

{{interactive_demo:1}}

<details><summary>Click to reveal the proof</summary>

The prefix collapses every input to $d$, so $\widetilde F(\mu)=F(d)$ and $\widetilde P(\mu)=P(d)$. Ablating the prefix changes nothing, because both stacks share it. Ablating an inner layer is masked by the forgetful top layer of $\widetilde F$. Replacing that top layer by the identity outputs $F(d)$ anyway.
</details>

Consequently, *any* rule that turns solo-ablation data into a damage estimate, and returns $0$ on an all-zero profile, certifies $0$ for some stack pair whose damage is $1$ at every input.

{{algorithm:2}}

## 5. What finite measurements *can* do

**Trajectory costs are sound per input.** Run the intact network on $\mu$. At each layer, also apply the pruned layer to the intact activations, and add up the per-layer distances. This sum $T(F,P,\mu)$ bounds $\operatorname{tv}(F(\mu),P(\mu))$.

**Extrapolation costs an $\ell^1$ factor.** If $\mu=\sum_ic_iw_i$ as vectors, then
$$\operatorname{tv}(F(\mu),P(\mu))\le\sum_i|c_i|\,T(F,P,w_i).$$

**Design budgets.** Given spanning probes with $\delta_a=\sum_ic_{a,i}s_i$, the budget $\sum_a\sum_i|c_{a,i}|\operatorname{tv}(s_if,s_ip)$ is probe-local, calibrated and sound.

<details><summary>Click to reveal the proofs</summary>

*Trajectory bound:* by induction, $\operatorname{tv}(F'(\mu f),P'(\mu p))\le\operatorname{tv}(F'(\mu f),P'(\mu f))+\operatorname{tv}(P'(\mu f),P'(\mu p))$. The first term is handled by induction and the second by the data-processing inequality.

*Combination inequality:* $vf-vp=\sum_ic_i(s_if-s_ip)$, followed by the triangle inequality. Applied to the composite channels of the stacks, it gives extrapolation. Applied at $v=\delta_a$, it shows that the design budget dominates every $\operatorname{tv}(f(a),p(a))$, so Theorem 1 gives soundness.
</details>

{{algorithm:1}}

The price of a design is its **amplification** $\max_a\sum_i|c_{a,i}|$. Point masses cost $1$. On two states, the window $\{(3/4,1/4),(1/4,3/4)\}$ costs $2$, since $\delta_0=\tfrac32\beta_{1/4}-\tfrac12\beta_{3/4}$. Interior probes cost more and more as they approach the centre:

## 7. Where this leads

* **Optimal interior designs.** It is conjectured that, among designs whose probes give each state probability at least $\eta$, the best amplification is $(1+(k-2)\eta)/(1-k\eta)$, attained by shrinking the simplex vertices uniformly. You can test this conjecture in the Probe Lab with the shrunk-vertex slider.
* **Epistatic factors.** Along the pruned trajectory, perturbations seem to be paid with odd weights $2(n-1-j)+1$.
* **Infinite state spaces.** No finite probe set spans, and it is conjectured that no finite probe set supports a sound, calibrated budget.

**Bottom line:** a sum of per-layer errors is a guarantee only when each term is a worst case. Held-out measurements become bounds only through a spanning design, and only after paying that design's amplification.

/-!
# Which probes?  Trajectory budgets and design coefficients

The dichotomy (`probe_budget_dichotomy`) says a probe set supports a sound
budget iff it spans.  This file makes the positive side *quantitative and
constructive*, which is what an experimental programme needs, and pins down the
exact boundary of the negative side.

## Trajectory budgets (the sharp edge of the dichotomy)

* `joint_le_trajectoryCost` — for a **fixed input** `μ`, the joint damage is at
  most the sum of the layer-output perturbations measured at the **intact
  upstream states of that same input**.  So a per-layer measurement taken on the
  input's own intact trajectory *is* sound for that input; what fails is reusing
  it for other inputs.
* `trajectory_window_dichotomy` — zero trajectory cost on every input of a
  held-out window certifies zero damage on **all** inputs iff the window spans.

## Design coefficients (the positive side, made quantitative)

* `tv_push_le_combination` — if `v = Σ cᵢ sᵢ` as signed measures, the
  perturbation of a layer at `v` is at most `Σ |cᵢ|` times its perturbations at
  the probes `sᵢ`;
* `designBudget_sound` — given probes `s` and coefficients `c` writing every
  Dirac state as `Σ c a i • s i`, the **design budget**
  `Σ_a Σ_i |c a i| · tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i))` is probe-local,
  calibrated and sound: an explicit sound budget computed from probe
  measurements only;
* `window_extrapolation` — the same coefficients extrapolate joint damage from a
  held-out window to any input in its span, with amplification `Σ |cᵢ|`.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Trajectory costs -/

/-- The trajectory cost of a stack pair at input `μ`: layer `j` is charged the
perturbation of its *own output* at the intact upstream state of `μ`. -/
def trajectoryCost : List (Kern α α) → List (Kern α α) → Dist α → ℚ
  | f :: F, p :: P, μ => tv (push f μ) (push p μ) + trajectoryCost F P (push f μ)
  | _, _, _ => 0

@[simp] theorem trajectoryCost_cons (f p : Kern α α) (F P : List (Kern α α)) (μ : Dist α) :
    trajectoryCost (f :: F) (p :: P) μ = tv (push f μ) (push p μ) + trajectoryCost F P (push f μ) :=
  rfl

/-- **Trajectory bound.**  At a fixed input, joint damage is at most the sum of the
per-layer output perturbations measured along the intact trajectory of that
input.  (Compare `chain_hybrid_bound`, which measures along the *pruned*
trajectory, inaccessible to an experimenter who only runs the intact model.) -/
theorem joint_le_trajectoryCost :
    ∀ (F P : List (Kern α α)), F.length = P.length →
      ∀ μ : Dist α, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) ≤ trajectoryCost F P μ := by
  intro F
  induction F with
  | nil => intro P hlen μ; cases P with
    | nil => simp [trajectoryCost]
    | cons p P => simp at hlen
  | cons f F ih =>
      intro P hlen μ
      cases P with
      | nil => simp at hlen
      | cons p P =>
          rw [chain_cons, chain_cons, trajectoryCost_cons]
          have h1 := tv_triangle (chain F (push f μ)) (chain P (push f μ)) (chain P (push p μ))
          have h2 := ih P (by simpa using hlen) (push f μ)
          have h3 := tv_chain_le P (push f μ) (push p μ)
          linarith

/-- Zero trajectory cost forces zero damage at that input. -/
theorem chain_eq_of_trajectoryCost_eq_zero (F P : List (Kern α α)) (hlen : F.length = P.length)
    (μ : Dist α) (h : trajectoryCost F P μ = 0) : chain F μ = chain P μ := by
  have := joint_le_trajectoryCost F P hlen μ
  rw [h] at this
  exact (tv_eq_zero_iff _ _).1 (le_antisymm this (tv_nonneg _ _))

/-- **Trajectory-window dichotomy.**  Requiring every pruned layer to reproduce its
intact counterpart along the intact trajectories of a held-out window certifies
the pruned stack on *all* inputs iff the window spans (or `α` is trivial).
Held-out-window measurements are sound *on the window*
(`joint_le_trajectoryCost`); they extrapolate exactly when the window spans. -/
theorem trajectory_window_dichotomy [DecidableEq α] (W : Set (Dist α)) :
    (∀ F P : List (Kern α α), F.length = P.length →
        (∀ w ∈ W, trajectoryCost F P w = 0) → ∀ μ : Dist α, chain F μ = chain P μ) ↔
      Subsingleton α ∨ Spans W := by
  rw [← window_certifies_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [window_certifies_iff, ← separates_iff]
    intro g q hgq
    funext a
    have := h [g] [q] rfl (fun w hw => by simp [trajectoryCost, hgq w hw]) (dirac a)
    simpa using this
  · intro h F P hlen hW μ
    exact h F P (fun w hw => chain_eq_of_trajectoryCost_eq_zero F P hlen w (hW w hw)) μ

/-! ## 2. Signed combinations of probes -/

/-- **Combination inequality.**  If `v.p = Σᵢ cᵢ • (s i).p`, then the perturbation
of a layer at `v` is controlled by its perturbations at the probes, weighted by
`|cᵢ|`. -/
theorem tv_push_le_combination {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f p : Kern α α) (s : ι → Dist α)
    (c : ι → ℚ) (v : Dist α) (hv : v.p = ∑ i, c i • (s i).p) :
    tv (push f v) (push p v) ≤ ∑ i, |c i| * tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i)) := by
  have hdiff : ∀ b, (push f v).p b - (push p v).p b
      = ∑ i, c i * ((push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b) := by
    intro b
    have e1 : (push f v).p b = ∑ i, c i * (push f (s i)).p b := by
      rw [← pushL_dist, hv, map_sum]
      simp only [map_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, pushL_dist]
    have e2 : (push p v).p b = ∑ i, c i * (push p (s i)).p b := by
      rw [← pushL_dist, hv, map_sum]
      simp only [map_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, pushL_dist]
    rw [e1, e2, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
  have hb : ∀ b, |(push f v).p b - (push p v).p b|
      ≤ ∑ i, |c i| * |(push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b| := by
    intro b
    rw [hdiff b]
    refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => abs_mul _ _
  unfold tv
  have hsum := Finset.sum_le_sum fun b (_ : b ∈ Finset.univ) => hb b
  rw [Finset.sum_comm] at hsum
  have : ∑ i, |c i| * ((∑ b, |(push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b|) / 2)
      = (∑ i, ∑ b, |c i| * |(push f (s i)).p b - (push p (s i)).p b|) / 2 := by
    rw [Finset.sum_div]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [mul_div_assoc', Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [this]
  linarith

/-! ## 3. Design budgets -/

/-- The design budget of a probe family `s` with Dirac-representing coefficients
`c`: computed from the probe responses only. -/
def designBudget {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (s : ι → Dist α) (c : α → ι → ℚ)
    (f p : Kern α α) : ℚ :=
  ∑ a, ∑ i, |c a i| * tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i))

/-- **Constructive sufficiency.**  If the coefficients `c` write every Dirac state
as a signed combination of the probes, the design budget is probe-local,
calibrated and sound. -/
theorem designBudget_sound [DecidableEq α] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (s : ι → Dist α)
    (c : α → ι → ℚ) (hc : ∀ a, (dirac a).p = ∑ i, c a i • (s i).p) :
    ProbeLocal (Set.range s) (designBudget s c) ∧ Calibrated (designBudget s c) ∧
      SoundBudget (designBudget s c) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro f p f' p' hf hp
    unfold designBudget
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [hf (s i) ⟨i, rfl⟩, hp (s i) ⟨i, rfl⟩]
  · intro f; simp [designBudget]
  · refine budget_sound_of_dominates _ fun f p a => ?_
    have h1 := tv_push_le_combination f p s (c a) (dirac a) (hc a)
    rw [push_dirac, push_dirac] at h1
    refine h1.trans ?_
    exact Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun a => ∑ i, |c a i| * tv (push f (s i)) (push p (s i)))
      (fun a _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => mul_nonneg (abs_nonneg _) (tv_nonneg _ _))
      (Finset.mem_univ a)

/-- With the Dirac probes and identity coefficients the design budget is the
Dirac-sum budget: the canonical design. -/
theorem designBudget_dirac [DecidableEq α] (f p : Kern α α) :
    designBudget (dirac : α → Dist α) (fun a i => if a = i then 1 else 0) f p
      = diracSumBudget f p := by
  unfold designBudget diracSumBudget
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a] <;> simp +contextual [push_dirac, eq_comm]

/-- **Window extrapolation.**  If an input `μ` is a signed combination
`Σ cᵢ wᵢ` of held-out window inputs, its joint damage is at most `Σ |cᵢ|` times
the trajectory costs measured on the window.  The `ℓ¹` size of the coefficients
is the amplification factor of the probe design. -/
theorem window_extrapolation [DecidableEq α] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (F P : List (Kern α α)) (hlen : F.length = P.length) (w : ι → Dist α) (c : ι → ℚ)
    (μ : Dist α) (hμ : μ.p = ∑ i, c i • (w i).p) :
    tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) ≤ ∑ i, |c i| * trajectoryCost F P (w i) := by
  rw [chain_eq_push_chainK, chain_eq_push_chainK]
  refine (tv_push_le_combination _ _ w c μ hμ).trans ?_
  refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (abs_nonneg _)
  rw [← chain_eq_push_chainK, ← chain_eq_push_chainK]
  exact joint_le_trajectoryCost F P hlen (w i)

/-!
# The probe-budget dichotomy

A per-layer budget functional `B` *depends only on the behaviour of a layer at
the probe states `S`* (`ProbeLocal S B`) if `B f p = B f' p'` whenever `f, f'`
and `p, p'` have the same responses at every probe.  It is *calibrated* if an
unpruned layer is charged nothing (`B f f = 0`).  Local + calibrated implies
*probe-blind*: a layer pair whose probe responses agree is charged `0`.

Main results:

* `blind_budget_counterexample` — if the probes do not span `ℚ^α` (and `α` has
  two points), then for **every** probe-blind budget and **every** depth `n+1`
  there is a stack pair whose total budget is `0` and whose joint damage, from
  some input, is `1`;
* `blind_budget_not_relaxed_sound` — no multiplicative or additive slack
  (`joint ≤ C · Σ budgets + δ`, `δ < 1`) repairs such a budget;
* `probe_budget_dichotomy` — **there is a sound, calibrated, `S`-local budget
  iff `α` is a singleton or `S` spans**;
* `window_certifies_iff` — a held-out window of inputs on which two stacks agree
  certifies agreement on *all* inputs iff the window spans;
* `small_window_never_certifies` — a window with fewer inputs than states never
  certifies anything: some stack pair is invisible on the window and maximally
  damaged off it.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Probe-local budget functionals -/

/-- `B` depends on a layer pair only through the responses at the probe states. -/
def ProbeLocal (S : Set (Dist α)) (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f p f' p' : Kern α α, AgreeOn S f f' → AgreeOn S p p' → B f p = B f' p'

/-- An unpruned layer is charged nothing. -/
def Calibrated (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop := ∀ f : Kern α α, B f f = 0

/-- A layer pair that no probe can tell apart is charged nothing. -/
def ProbeBlind (S : Set (Dist α)) (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f p : Kern α α, AgreeOn S f p → B f p = 0

/-- Probe-local calibrated budgets are probe-blind. -/
theorem ProbeLocal.blind {S : Set (Dist α)} {B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ}
    (hL : ProbeLocal S B) (hC : Calibrated B) : ProbeBlind S B := by
  intro f p hfp
  rw [hL f p f f (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun s hs => (hfp s hs).symm)]
  exact hC f

/-! ## 2. Stacks built from a witness layer -/

theorem diracProbes_suffice [DecidableEq α] :
    ∃ B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ,

# Per-layer budgets: soundness is exactly uniform domination

`Probability.NET59HybridEpistasis` proves that a per-layer perturbation bound
that is *uniform over upstream states* adds up along depth
(`chain_tv_le_depth_mul`), and `Probability.NET59NonIdentifiability` shows that a

observations into an exact characterisation.

A **per-layer budget functional** is any map `B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ`
assigning a number to an (intact, pruned) layer pair.  It is **sound** if for
every pair of stacks of equal depth and every input law, the joint damage is at
most the sum of the per-layer budgets.

Main results:

* `budget_sound_of_dominates` — if `B f p ≥ tv (f a) (p a)` for every state `a`
  then `B` is sound (heterogeneous depth-additivity, generalising
  `chain_tv_le_depth_mul`);
* `dominates_of_budget_sound` — conversely every sound budget dominates the
  pointwise channel distance at every state (single-layer stacks with Dirac
  inputs);
* `budget_sound_iff_dominates` — **soundness ⇔ uniform domination**;
* `uniformBudget` (the worst case over states) is sound and is the *least*
  sound budget: `budget_sound_iff_uniform_le`.

is literally the definition of a sound budget.

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Small facts about channels -/

/-- Pushing a Dirac mass through a channel evaluates the channel. -/
@[simp] theorem push_dirac [DecidableEq α] (K : Kern α α) (a : α) : push K (dirac a) = K a := by
  refine Dist.ext' fun b => ?_
  simp only [push_apply, dirac]
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a] <;> simp +contextual

/-- Sequential composition of two channels: first `K`, then `G`. -/
def compK (K G : Kern α α) : Kern α α := fun a => push G (K a)

/-- Pushing twice is pushing through the composite channel. -/
theorem push_push (K G : Kern α α) (μ : Dist α) : push G (push K μ) = push (compK K G) μ := by
  refine Dist.ext' fun b => ?_
  simp only [push_apply, compK, Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => by ring

/-- The channel computed by a whole stack. -/
def chainK [DecidableEq α] (L : List (Kern α α)) : Kern α α := fun a => chain L (dirac a)

/-- A stack acts on input laws as the single channel `chainK L`: running a stack
is linear in the input law. -/
theorem chain_eq_push_chainK [DecidableEq α] (L : List (Kern α α)) (μ : Dist α) :
    chain L μ = push (chainK L) μ := by
  induction L generalizing μ with
  | nil =>
      have : chainK ([] : List (Kern α α)) = idK := rfl
      rw [this, push_idK, chain_nil]
  | cons K L ih =>

        funext a
        simp only [chainK, compK, chain_cons, push_dirac]
        exact ih (K a)
      rw [chain_cons, ih, push_push, hK]

/-! ## 2. Budget functionals -/

/-- The total budget charged to a pair of stacks: the sum of the per-layer
budgets, layer by layer. -/
def budgetSum (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : List (Kern α α) → List (Kern α α) → ℚ
  | f :: F, p :: P => B f p + budgetSum B F P
  | _, _ => 0

@[simp] theorem budgetSum_cons (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) (f p : Kern α α)
    (F P : List (Kern α α)) : budgetSum B (f :: F) (p :: P) = B f p + budgetSum B F P := rfl

@[simp] theorem budgetSum_nil (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) (P : List (Kern α α)) :
    budgetSum B [] P = 0 := by cases P <;> rfl

/-- A per-layer budget functional is **sound** if, on every pair of stacks of
equal depth and from every input law, the joint damage never exceeds the sum of
the per-layer budgets. -/
def SoundBudget (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ F P : List (Kern α α), F.length = P.length →
    ∀ μ : Dist α, tv (chain F μ) (chain P μ) ≤ budgetSum B F P

pointwise channel distance. -/

    (hB : ∀ f p : Kern α α, ∀ a, tv (f a) (p a) ≤ B f p) :
    ∀ (F P : List (Kern α α)) (μ : Dist α), hybridCost F P μ ≤ budgetSum B F P := by
  intro F
  induction F with
  | nil => intro P μ; simp
  | cons f F ih =>
      intro P μ
      cases P with
      | nil => simp [hybridCost, budgetSum]
      | cons p P =>
          rw [hybridCost_cons, budgetSum_cons]

            tv_push_perturb_unif f p μ (hB f p)
          have h2 := ih P (push p μ)
          linarith

the channel distance at *every* state is sound. -/
theorem budget_sound_of_dominates (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ)
    (hB : ∀ f p : Kern α α, ∀ a, tv (f a) (p a) ≤ B f p) : SoundBudget B := by
  intro F P hlen μ
  exact (chain_hybrid_bound F P hlen μ).trans (hybridCost_le_budgetSum B hB F P μ)

/-- **Necessity.**  A sound budget must dominate the channel distance at every
single state: test it on the depth-one stack fed with a Dirac input. -/
theorem dominates_of_budget_sound [DecidableEq α] (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ)
    (hB : SoundBudget B) (f p : Kern α α) (a : α) : tv (f a) (p a) ≤ B f p := by
  have h := hB [f] [p] rfl (dirac a)
  simpa [budgetSum] using h

/-- **Soundness is exactly uniform domination.** -/
theorem budget_sound_iff_dominates [DecidableEq α] (B : Kern α α → Kern α α → ℚ) :
    SoundBudget B ↔ ∀ f p : Kern α α, ∀ a, tv (f a) (p a) ≤ B f p :=
  ⟨fun h => dominates_of_budget_sound B h, budget_sound_of_dominates B⟩

/-! ## 3. The uniform budget is the least sound budget -/

/-- The uniform (worst-case over states) per-layer budget. -/
def uniformBudget [Nonempty α] (f p : Kern α α) : ℚ :=
  Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty fun a => tv (f a) (p a)

theorem le_uniformBudget [Nonempty α] (f p : Kern α α) (a : α) :
    tv (f a) (p a) ≤ uniformBudget f p :=
  Finset.le_sup' (fun a => tv (f a) (p a)) (Finset.mem_univ a)

/-- The uniform budget is attained at some state. -/
theorem exists_uniformBudget_eq [Nonempty α] (f p : Kern α α) :
    ∃ a, tv (f a) (p a) = uniformBudget f p := by
  obtain ⟨a, -, ha⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := α))

  exact ⟨a, ha.symm⟩

  budget_sound_of_dominates _ le_uniformBudget

theorem budget_sound_iff_uniform_le [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]

    exact (le_uniformBudget f p a).trans (h f p)

          have h2 := ih P (by simpa using hlen) (fun q hq => h q (by simp [hq]))

          push_cast [List.length_cons]
          linarith

/-!
# Masking suffixes: every pruning instance hides from every solo probe

`Probability.NET59NonIdentifiability` exhibits one witness family
(`fullStack` / `prunedStack` on `Fin 2`, probed at the single input `d0`) whose
solo profile vanishes while the joint damage is any prescribed `t`.  Here the
construction is turned into a *universal transformation*.

`maskStack F d` / `maskPruned P d` wrap an arbitrary intact stack `F` and pruned
stack `P` between

* a **collapsing prefix** `constK d` (shared by both stacks), which sends every
  upstream state to the probe state `d`, and
* a **masking suffix**: the intact stack ends with the forgetful layer
  `constK (chain F d)`, the pruned stack with the transparent layer `idK`.

`masking_suffix` proves, for **every** input law `μ` (so in particular for every
finite or infinite set of probe inputs, spanning or not):

* the joint damage of the wrapped pair equals the original joint damage
  `tv (chain F d) (chain P d)`, and
* the solo profile of the wrapped pair is identically `0`.

— at any number of probe inputs — can bound joint damage
(`solo_certificate_unsound`).  Every pruning instance, however damaging, can be
made invisible to solo probing at the cost of two extra layers.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-- The wrapped intact stack: collapse to `d`, run `F`, then forget everything
and output the intact answer `chain F d`. -/
def maskStack (F : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) : List (Kern α α) :=
  constK d :: (F ++ [constK (chain F d)])

/-- The wrapped pruned stack: collapse to `d`, run `P`, then pass through. -/
def maskPruned [DecidableEq α] (P : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) : List (Kern α α) :=
  constK d :: (P ++ [idK])

theorem length_maskStack (F : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) :
    (maskStack F d).length = F.length + 2 := by simp [maskStack]

theorem length_maskPruned [DecidableEq α] (P : List (Kern α α)) (d : Dist α) :
    (maskPruned P d).length = P.length + 2 := by simp [maskPruned]

/-- The wrapped intact stack outputs `chain F d` from every input. -/
theorem chain_maskStack (F : List (Kern α α)) (d μ : Dist α) :
    chain (maskStack F d) μ = chain F d := by
  rw [maskStack, chain_cons, chain_snoc_constK]

/-- The wrapped pruned stack outputs `chain P d` from every input. -/
theorem chain_maskPruned [DecidableEq α] (P : List (Kern α α)) (d μ : Dist α) :
    chain (maskPruned P d) μ = chain P d := by
  rw [maskPruned, chain_cons, push_constK, chain_append, chain_cons, chain_nil, push_idK]

    rw [chain_cons, chain_snoc_constK]

/-!
# Which probe sets see a layer?  The linear algebra of probing

A budget that "depends only on the behaviour of a layer at prescribed upstream
states" sees a channel `K` only through the probe responses `push K s`,
`s ∈ S`.  Because `push K` is *linear* in the input law, what a probe set can
see is governed by the linear span of the probe vectors `s.p ∈ ℚ^α`.

* `separates_of_spans` — if the probe vectors span `ℚ^α`, two channels with the
  same probe responses are equal;
* `exists_blind_pair` — **witness interpolation**: if the probe vectors do *not*
  span `ℚ^α` (and `α` has two points), there are two channels with identical
  responses at *every* probe whose outputs at some state are mutually singular
  (`tv = 1`).  The construction takes a nonzero linear functional `φ`
  annihilating the probes, normalises its coefficient vector `w` to `u` with
  `max |u| = 1`, and mixes two point masses with weights `(1 ± u a)/2`;
* `separates_iff` — a probe set separates channels **iff** `α` is a singleton
  or the probes span;
* `diracProbes_spans`, `card_le_of_spans` — the `|α|` Dirac probes span, and no
  family of fewer than `|α|` probes does.  So a finite probe set that suffices
  exists, and its minimum size is exactly the number of states.
-/

namespace Catalog.Probability.NET59.ProbeBudgets

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α]

/-! ## 1. Probe vectors and their span -/

/-- The span of the probe vectors `s.p` of a set of probe states. -/
def probeSpan (S : Set (Dist α)) : Submodule ℚ (α → ℚ) := Submodule.span ℚ (Dist.p '' S)

/-- A probe set *spans* if its probe vectors span all of `ℚ^α`. -/
def Spans (S : Set (Dist α)) : Prop := probeSpan S = ⊤

/-- Two channels *agree on* a probe set if they have the same response at every
probe state. -/
def AgreeOn (S : Set (Dist α)) (f p : Kern α α) : Prop := ∀ s ∈ S, push f s = push p s

/-- A probe set *separates* channels if agreeing on it forces equality. -/
def Separates (S : Set (Dist α)) : Prop := ∀ f p : Kern α α, AgreeOn S f p → f = p

/-- The pushforward through a channel, extended linearly to all of `ℚ^α`. -/
def pushL (K : Kern α α) : (α → ℚ) →ₗ[ℚ] (α → ℚ) where
  toFun v b := ∑ a, v a * (K a).p b
  map_add' v w := by
    funext b; simp only [Pi.add_apply, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  map_smul' c v := by
    funext b; simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]

theorem pushL_dist (K : Kern α α) (s : Dist α) : pushL K s.p = (push K s).p := rfl

theorem pushL_single [DecidableEq α] (K : Kern α α) (a : α) :
    pushL K (fun x => if x = a then 1 else 0) = (K a).p := by
  funext b
  change ∑ x, (if x = a then (1 : ℚ) else 0) * (K x).p b = (K a).p b
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a] <;> simp +contextual

/-- **Spanning probes see everything.**  If the probe vectors span `ℚ^α`, two

theorem separates_of_spans {S : Set (Dist α)} (hS : Spans S) : Separates S := by

  simp only [dirac]

/-! ## 5. The separation dichotomy -/

/-- On a singleton state space there is only one law. -/
theorem dist_subsingleton [Subsingleton α] (μ ν : Dist α) : μ = ν := by
  refine Dist.ext' fun a => ?_
  have hμ := μ.sum_one; have hν := ν.sum_one
  rw [Fintype.sum_subsingleton _ a] at hμ hν
  rw [hμ, hν]

/-- **Separation dichotomy.**  A set of probe states determines every channel
from its probe responses if and only if the state space is a singleton or the
probe vectors span `ℚ^α`. -/
theorem separates_iff [DecidableEq α] (S : Set (Dist α)) :
    Separates S ↔ Subsingleton α ∨ Spans S := by
  constructor
  · intro hsep
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    obtain ⟨hns, hspan⟩ := h
    obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := exists_pair_ne α

  · rintro (h | h)
    · intro f p _; funext a; exact dist_subsingleton _ _

/-- The `|α|` Dirac probes span. -/
theorem diracProbes_spans [DecidableEq α] : Spans (Set.range (dirac : α → Dist α)) := by
  rw [Spans, eq_top_iff]
  intro v _
  have hv : v = ∑ a, v a • (dirac a).p := by

  exact Submodule.sum_mem _ fun a _ =>
    Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨dirac a, ⟨a, rfl⟩, rfl⟩)

/-- **Lower bound on probe budgets.**  A spanning family of probe states has at
least `|α|` members: no budget certified on fewer probes than states can see
every channel. -/
theorem card_le_of_spans {m : ℕ} (probes : Fin m → Dist α)
    (h : Spans (Set.range probes)) : Fintype.card α ≤ m := by
  have hrange : Dist.p '' Set.range probes = Set.range (fun i => (probes i).p) := by

  rw [h, finrank_top, Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card] at h1
  simpa using h1

  "future_directions": "# Future directions: probe-local per-layer budgets

This cycle established the following results.

* A per-layer budget is sound **if and only if** it dominates the worst-case perturbation over upstream states (the uniform budget is the least sound budget).
* A probe set supports a sound, calibrated, probe-local budget **if and only if** its probe vectors span $\mathbb{Q}^\alpha$, or $|\alpha| = 1$ (the probe-budget dichotomy). At least $|\alpha|$ probes are needed (the probe-count lower bound).
* Every pruning instance can be hidden from output-level solo probing at every input by adding two layers (the masking-suffix theorem).
* Measurements taken along the input's own intact trajectory are sound for that input. They extrapolate to other inputs with amplification equal to the $\ell^1$ norm of the coefficients that express those inputs in terms of the window (window extrapolation; soundness of design budgets).

The conjectures below build on these results.

## 1. Optimal amplification of interior probe designs

**Conjecture.** Let $|\alpha| = k$ and suppose every probe is an $\eta$-interior input, meaning each state has probability at least $\eta$, with $0 \le \eta < 1/k$. Take the smallest possible value, over spanning probe families and coefficient choices, of $\max_a \sum_i |c_{a,i}|$. This value is exactly $(1 + (k-2)\eta)/(1 - k\eta)$. It is attained by the shrunk vertices $(1-k\eta)\delta_a + \eta\mathbf{1}$.

The key insight is that the design budget's amplification is the $\ell^1$ norm of the coefficients expressing the vertices of the simplex in terms of the probes. So the best design is a polytope-inscription problem in the simplex.

Why now? The soundness theorem for design budgets turns any spanning probe family into an explicit sound budget. Deployment probes are always interior: real inputs are never Dirac masses. The constant in front of the budget is therefore the one quantity left to optimise.

## 2. Epistatic factor law along the pruned trajectory

**Conjecture.** For stacks of depth $n$, the hybrid cost along the pruned trajectory satisfies $\text{hybridCost} \le \sum_j (2(n-1-j)+1)\cdot \text{point}_j$, where $\text{point}_j$ is the perturbation on the intact trajectory. The odd factors $2(n-1-j)+1$ are tight. Depth 2 gives the factor $3$ already established for two-layer stacks.

The key insight is that each upstream perturbation is paid once directly and then again, twice, through context shift at every downstream layer. Repeated use of the context-shift inequality telescopes into odd weights.

Why now? The trajectory bound showed that intact-trajectory costs bound the joint damage with factor $1$, while the hybrid bound needs the pruned trajectory. The gap between the two accountings is exactly this epistatic factor.

## 3. No finite probe set on infinite state spaces

**Conjecture.** For channels on an infinite standard Borel space, no finite set of probe laws supports a sound, calibrated, probe-local budget. More strongly, a probe set supports one if and only if its linear span is weak-$*$ dense in the bounded signed measures.

Necessity of Uniform Per-Layer Budgets -- numerical companion.

Everything is exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction), so every

Setting
-------
* A finite state space {0, ..., k-1}.
* A *law* is a probability vector of length k.
* A *channel* (layer) K is a row-stochastic k x k matrix: row a is the law K(a).
* push(K, mu) = mu K  (run one layer on an input law).
* A *stack* is a list of channels applied left to right.
* tv(mu, nu) = (1/2) * sum_b |mu_b - nu_b|  (total variation distance).

Sections
--------
 1. Soundness  <=>  uniform domination      (depth-additivity and its converse)
 2. Single-state certificates fail          (blind pairs for any non-spanning probe set)
 3. The probe-budget dichotomy              (spanning probe sets, probe count >= k)

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

Law = List[Fraction]
Channel = List[Law]          # row a = law K(a)
Stack = List[Channel]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic objects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def dirac(k: int, a: int) -> Law:
    """Point mass at state a."""
    return [Fraction(1) if b == a else Fraction(0) for b in range(k)]


def bern(t: Fraction) -> Law:
    """Two-state law putting mass t on state 1."""
    return [1 - t, t]


def push(K: Channel, mu: Sequence[Fraction]) -> Law:
    """Push a law (or any signed vector) through a channel: (mu K)_b = sum_a mu_a K(a)_b."""
    k = len(K)
    return [sum((mu[a] * K[a][b] for a in range(k)), Fraction(0)) for b in range(k)]


def chain(L: Stack, mu: Law) -> Law:
    """Run a whole stack on an input law."""
    for K in L:
        mu = push(K, mu)
    return mu


def tv(mu: Sequence[Fraction], nu: Sequence[Fraction]) -> Fraction:
    """Total variation distance (half the l1 distance)."""
    return sum((abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(mu, nu)), Fraction(0)) / 2


def identity(k: int) -> Channel:
    return [dirac(k, a) for a in range(k)]


def const_channel(d: Law) -> Channel:
    """The forgetful layer: every upstream state is sent to the law d."""
    return [list(d) for _ in range(len(d))]


def random_law(k: int, rng: random.Random, denom: int = 12) -> Law:
    w = [rng.randint(0, denom) for _ in range(k)]
    if sum(w) == 0:
        w[rng.randrange(k)] = 1
    s = sum(w)
    return [Fraction(x, s) for x in w]


def random_channel(k: int, rng: random.Random) -> Channel:
    return [random_law(k, rng) for _ in range(k)]


def perturb_channel(K: Channel, rng: random.Random, strength: Fraction) -> Channel:
    """Mix each row of K with a random law: a 'pruned' version of the layer."""
    k = len(K)
    out: Channel = []
    for row in K:
        r = random_law(k, rng)
        lam = strength * Fraction(rng.randint(0, 10), 10)
        out.append([(1 - lam) * x + lam * y for x, y in zip(row, r)])
    return out


def fmt(x: Fraction) -> str:
    return str(x) if x.denominator <= 1000 else f"{float(x):.6f}"


def fmt_law(mu: Sequence[Fraction]) -> str:
    return "(" + ", ".join(fmt(x) for x in mu) + ")"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def uniform_budget(f: Channel, p: Channel) -> Fraction:
    """Worst case over upstream states of the per-layer perturbation."""
    return max(tv(f[a], p[a]) for a in range(len(f)))


def single_state_budget(f: Channel, p: Channel, s: Law) -> Fraction:
    """A budget certified only at one probe law s."""
    return tv(push(f, s), push(p, s))


def budget_sum(budget, F: Stack, P: Stack) -> Fraction:
    return sum((budget(f, p) for f, p in zip(F, P)), Fraction(0))


def hybrid_cost(F: Stack, P: Stack, mu: Law) -> Fraction:
    """Per-layer perturbations measured along the *pruned* trajectory."""
    total = Fraction(0)
    for f, p in zip(F, P):
        total += tv(push(f, mu), push(p, mu))
        mu = push(p, mu)
    return total


def trajectory_cost(F: Stack, P: Stack, mu: Law) -> Fraction:
    """Per-layer perturbations measured along the *intact* trajectory."""
    total = Fraction(0)
    for f, p in zip(F, P):
        total += tv(push(f, mu), push(p, mu))
        mu = push(f, mu)
    return total


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exact linear algebra over Q
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def rank(rows: List[Law]) -> int:
    M = [list(r) for r in rows]
    if not M:
        return 0
    n_cols = len(M[0])
    r = 0
    for c in range(n_cols):
        piv = next((i for i in range(r, len(M)) if M[i][c] != 0), None)
        if piv is None:
            continue
        M[r], M[piv] = M[piv], M[r]
        for i in range(len(M)):
            if i != r and M[i][c] != 0:
                fac = M[i][c] / M[r][c]
                M[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(M[i], M[r])]
        r += 1
    return r


def annihilator(rows: List[Law], k: int) -> Optional[Law]:
    """A nonzero w with sum_a s_a w_a = 0 for every row s, or None if the rows span Q^k."""
    M = [list(r) for r in rows]
    pivots: List[int] = []
    r = 0
    for c in range(k):
        piv = next((i for i in range(r, len(M)) if M[i][c] != 0), None)
        if piv is None:
            continue
        M[r], M[piv] = M[piv], M[r]
        lead = M[r][c]
        M[r] = [x / lead for x in M[r]]
        for i in range(len(M)):
            if i != r and M[i][c] != 0:
                fac = M[i][c]
                M[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(M[i], M[r])]
        pivots.append(c)
        r += 1
    free = [c for c in range(k) if c not in pivots]
    if not free:
        return None
    fc = free[0]
    w = [Fraction(0)] * k
    w[fc] = Fraction(1)
    for i, pc in enumerate(pivots):
        w[pc] = -M[i][fc]
    return w


def solve_dirac_coefficients(probes: List[Law]) -> List[List[Fraction]]:
    """For k linearly independent probes, return c with dirac(a) = sum_i c[a][i] probes[i]."""
    k = len(probes)
    # Solve c S = I where S has the probes as rows: c = S^{-1}.
    A = [list(probes[i]) + dirac(k, i) for i in range(k)]   # augment [S | I], invert S
    for c in range(k):
        piv = next(i for i in range(c, k) if A[i][c] != 0)
        A[c], A[piv] = A[piv], A[c]
        lead = A[c][c]
        A[c] = [x / lead for x in A[c]]
        for i in range(k):
            if i != c and A[i][c] != 0:
                fac = A[i][c]
                A[i] = [x - fac * y for x, y in zip(A[i], A[c])]
    Sinv = [row[k:] for row in A]
    return Sinv  # row a of S^{-1} expresses dirac(a)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm: witness interpolation (the blind pair)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def blind_pair(probes: List[Law], k: int, x: int = 0, y: int = 1
               ) -> Optional[Tuple[Channel, Channel, int]]:
    """
    If the probe vectors do not span Q^k (and k >= 2), build two channels g, q that
    respond identically to every probe but whose outputs at some state a0 are
    mutually singular (tv = 1).  Returns (g, q, a0) or None if the probes span.
    """
    w = annihilator(probes, k)
    if w is None:
        return None
    a0 = max(range(k), key=lambda a: abs(w[a]))
    M = abs(w[a0])
    u = [wa / M for wa in w]                 # |u_a| <= 1, |u_{a0}| = 1
    dx, dy = dirac(k, x), dirac(k, y)
    g = [[(1 + u[a]) / 2 * dx[b] + (1 - u[a]) / 2 * dy[b] for b in range(k)] for a in range(k)]
    q = [[(1 - u[a]) / 2 * dx[b] + (1 + u[a]) / 2 * dy[b] for b in range(k)] for a in range(k)]
    return g, q, a0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm: masking suffix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def mask_stacks(F: Stack, P: Stack, d: Law) -> Tuple[Stack, Stack]:
    """Collapse to d, run the original stack, then forget (intact) / pass through (pruned)."""
    k = len(d)
    Fm = [const_channel(d)] + F + [const_channel(chain(F, d))]
    Pm = [const_channel(d)] + P + [identity(k)]
    return Fm, Pm


def solo_cost(F: Stack, P: Stack, mu: Law, j: int) -> Fraction:
    """Output-level damage of ablating layer j alone (replace F[j] by P[j])."""
    G = list(F)
    G[j] = P[j]
    return tv(chain(F, mu), chain(G, mu))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Design budget
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def design_budget(probes: List[Law], coeffs: List[List[Fraction]], f: Channel, p: Channel
                  ) -> Fraction:
    """sum_a sum_i |c[a][i]| * tv(push f s_i, push p s_i): computed from probe responses only."""
    resp = [tv(push(f, s), push(p, s)) for s in probes]
    return sum((abs(coeffs[a][i]) * resp[i]
                for a in range(len(coeffs)) for i in range(len(probes))), Fraction(0))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sections
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def section_1(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("1. Soundness <=> uniform domination (depth-additivity)")
    k = 3
    worst_ratio = Fraction(0)
    for trial in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 6)
        F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 3)) for f in F]
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        joint = tv(chain(F, mu), chain(P, mu))
        hyb = hybrid_cost(F, P, mu)
        ub = budget_sum(uniform_budget, F, P)
        assert joint <= hyb <= ub, "depth-additivity violated?!"
        if ub > 0:
            worst_ratio = max(worst_ratio, joint / ub)
    print("200 random stack pairs on 3 states, depths 1..6:")
    print("  joint damage <= hybrid cost <= sum of uniform budgets  held in every case.")
    print(f"  largest observed ratio joint / (sum of uniform budgets) = {fmt(worst_ratio)}")

    # Closed form n * eps
    eps = Fraction(1, 20)
    f = identity(2)
    p = [[1 - eps, eps], [eps, 1 - eps]]       # flips with probability eps
    for n in (1, 2, 5, 10):
        F, P = [f] * n, [p] * n
        joint = tv(chain(F, dirac(2, 0)), chain(P, dirac(2, 0)))
        print(f"  depth {n:2d}, each layer eps = 1/20 in the worst case: joint = {fmt(joint):>10}"
              f"  <= n*eps = {fmt(n * eps)}")

    # Necessity: the uniform budget is the least sound budget.
    f, p = random_channel(3, rng), random_channel(3, rng)
    a_star = max(range(3), key=lambda a: tv(f[a], p[a]))
    print(f"  Necessity: depth-one stack fed the Dirac input at state {a_star} has damage"
          f" {fmt(tv(f[a_star], p[a_star]))} = uniform budget {fmt(uniform_budget(f, p))}.")
    print("  So any budget charging less than the worst case is unsound on that one-layer stack.")


def section_2() -> None:
    banner("2. Single-state certificates fail: the blind pair")
    # The balanced probe on two states cannot tell identity from a flip.
    s = bern(Fraction(1, 2))
    idk = identity(2)
    flip = [dirac(2, 1), dirac(2, 0)]
    print(f"Probe s = {fmt_law(s)}.  push(id, s) = {fmt_law(push(idk, s))},"
          f" push(flip, s) = {fmt_law(push(flip, s))}")
    print(f"  but tv(id(0), flip(0)) = {fmt(tv(idk[0], flip[0]))}: a single-state budget charges 0,"
          " the damage at the Dirac input is 1.")

    # Witness interpolation through an arbitrary non-spanning probe set on 4 states.
    k = 4
    probes = [[Fraction(1, 4)] * 4,
              [Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6)],
              [Fraction(1, 10), Fraction(2, 10), Fraction(3, 10), Fraction(4, 10)]]
    print(f"\nNon-spanning probe set on {k} states (rank {rank(probes)} < {k}):")
    for pr in probes:
        print("   ", fmt_law(pr))
    res = blind_pair(probes, k)
    assert res is not None
    g, q, a0 = res
    for i, pr in enumerate(probes):
        rg, rq = push(g, pr), push(q, pr)
        assert rg == rq
        print(f"  probe {i}: g responds {fmt_law(rg)}, q responds {fmt_law(rq)}  (identical)")
    print(f"  but at state a0 = {a0}: g(a0) = {fmt_law(g[a0])}, q(a0) = {fmt_law(q[a0])},"
          f" tv = {fmt(tv(g[a0], q[a0]))}")

    # Any probe-blind budget: total budget 0 at every depth, damage 1.
    for n in (0, 3, 7):
        F = [g] + [identity(k)] * n
        P = [q] + [identity(k)] * n
        dmg = tv(chain(F, dirac(k, a0)), chain(P, dirac(k, a0)))
        print(f"  depth {n + 1}: every calibrated probe-local budget totals 0, joint damage = {fmt(dmg)}")


def section_3() -> None:
    banner("3. The probe-budget dichotomy: spanning is necessary and sufficient")
    k = 3
    families = {
        "one interior probe": [[Fraction(1, 3)] * 3],
        "two probes": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
                       [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)]],
        "three interior probes": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
                                  [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)],
                                  [Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(2, 3)]],
        "three probes, dependent": [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0)],
                                    [Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2)],
                                    [Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4)]],
        "the 3 Dirac probes": [dirac(3, a) for a in range(3)],
    }
    for name, probes in families.items():
        r = rank(probes)
        verdict = "SPANS  -> a sound calibrated probe-local budget exists" if r == k else \
            "fails  -> every calibrated probe-local budget is unsound"
        print(f"  {name:26s} rank {r}/{k}: {verdict}")
        if r < k:
            res = blind_pair(probes, k)
            assert res is not None
            g, q, a0 = res
            assert all(push(g, s) == push(q, s) for s in probes)
            assert tv(g[a0], q[a0]) == 1
    print("  Note the dependent family: three probes are not enough unless they are independent;")
    print("  fewer than k = 3 probes never suffice.")


def section_4(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("4. Masking suffix: every pruning instance hides from solo probing")
    k = 3
    F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(3)]
    P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1)) for f in F]
    d = random_law(k, rng)
    original = tv(chain(F, d), chain(P, d))
    Fm, Pm = mask_stacks(F, P, d)
    print(f"Original depth-3 pair, probe state d = {fmt_law(d)}: joint damage at d = {fmt(original)}")
    print("  original solo costs at d:",
          ", ".join(fmt(solo_cost(F, P, d, j)) for j in range(3)))
    for trial in range(3):
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        joint = tv(chain(Fm, mu), chain(Pm, mu))
        solos = [solo_cost(Fm, Pm, mu, j) for j in range(len(Fm))]
        assert joint == original and all(sc == 0 for sc in solos)
        print(f"  masked (depth 5) at input {fmt_law(mu)}: joint = {fmt(joint)},"
              f" solo costs = {[fmt(sc) for sc in solos]}")

    # The NET-59 numbers: two states, probe d0, target 17/1000.
    t = Fraction(17, 1000)
    d0 = dirac(2, 0)
    n = 2
    F = [identity(2)] * (n + 1)
    P = [const_channel(bern(t))] * (n + 1)
    Fm, Pm = mask_stacks(F, P, d0)
    mu = bern(Fraction(2, 3))
    print(f"\n  Witness family on 2 states, depth {len(Fm)}: joint damage at {fmt_law(mu)} ="
          f" {fmt(tv(chain(Fm, mu), chain(Pm, mu)))}, solo profile ="
          f" {[fmt(solo_cost(Fm, Pm, mu, j)) for j in range(len(Fm))]}")


def section_5(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("5. Trajectory costs: sound on the window, extrapolate only through the span")
    k = 3
    viol = 0
    for _ in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        F = [random_channel(k, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 2)) for f in F]
        mu = random_law(k, rng)
        if tv(chain(F, mu), chain(P, mu)) > trajectory_cost(F, P, mu):
            viol += 1
    print(f"  200 random pairs: joint damage <= intact-trajectory cost violated {viol} times.")

    # Window extrapolation on two states, window {bern 1/4, bern 3/4}.
    w1, w2 = bern(Fraction(1, 4)), bern(Fraction(3, 4))
    c = [Fraction(3, 2), Fraction(-1, 2)]
    comb = [c[0] * w1[b] + c[1] * w2[b] for b in range(2)]
    print(f"  d0 = 3/2 * bern(1/4) - 1/2 * bern(3/4) = {fmt_law(comb)}   (l1 amplification 2)")
    worst = Fraction(0)
    for _ in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        F = [random_channel(2, rng) for _ in range(n)]
        P = [perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1, 2)) for f in F]
        lhs = tv(chain(F, dirac(2, 0)), chain(P, dirac(2, 0)))
        rhs = abs(c[0]) * trajectory_cost(F, P, w1) + abs(c[1]) * trajectory_cost(F, P, w2)
        assert lhs <= rhs
        if rhs > 0:
            worst = max(worst, lhs / rhs)
    print(f"  extrapolated bound held on 200 random pairs; tightest ratio = {fmt(worst)}")


def section_6(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    banner("6. Design budgets: an explicit sound budget from probe measurements")
    probes = [[Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)],
              [Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(1, 5)],
              [Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(1, 6), Fraction(2, 3)]]
    C = solve_dirac_coefficients(probes)
    for a in range(3):
        recon = [sum((C[a][i] * probes[i][b] for i in range(3)), Fraction(0)) for b in range(3)]
        assert recon == dirac(3, a)
        print(f"  dirac({a}) = " + " + ".join(f"({fmt(C[a][i])})*s{i}" for i in range(3))
              + f"   amplification {fmt(sum(abs(x) for x in C[a]))}")
    for _ in range(300):
        f = random_channel(3, rng)
        p = perturb_channel(f, rng, Fraction(1))
        assert design_budget(probes, C, f, p) >= uniform_budget(f, p)
    print("  design budget >= uniform budget on 300 random layer pairs  (hence sound).")

    print("\n  Amplification of the symmetric two-state design {bern(eta), bern(1-eta)}:")
    for eta in (Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 10), Fraction(1, 4), Fraction(2, 5), Fraction(9, 20)):
        Cd = solve_dirac_coefficients([bern(eta), bern(1 - eta)])
        amp = max(sum(abs(x) for x in row) for row in Cd)
        print(f"    eta = {fmt(eta):>5}: max_a sum_i |c_ai| = {fmt(amp):>4}   (1/(1-2 eta) = {fmt(1 / (1 - 2 * eta))})")


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(59)
    section_1(rng)
    section_2()
    section_3()
    section_4(rng)
    section_5(rng)
    section_6(rng)
    print("\nAll checks passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
